lessons.heading: The image
lessons.body: Orthodox teaching allows Christ to be depicted because the Word truly became visible in the flesh. An icon witnesses to the one depicted.

lessons.heading: The distinction
lessons.body: Nicaea II distinguishes the honor given to an icon from worship, which belongs to God alone. John 1:14 anchors the argument in the incarnation.

lessons.heading: The Father
lessons.body: St John of Damascus defended holy images by pointing to the God who had become visible in human life.

lessons.heading: The holy icons
lessons.body: An icon is not decoration and not a visual aid you may take or leave. Orthodox Christians pray before it, kiss it, and treat it as holy. That honor has been attacked more than once, and the Church answered by refusing both idolatry and the ban on images of the incarnate Lord. Fr Paul Florensky’s line is the one to keep: the icon is a window onto the other world. Through it a person comes into contact with the spiritual world and with those who live there. The wood is not God. The person shown is truly approached. Veneration passes to the prototype; worship stays with God.

All materials are divine

questions.prompt: What is an icon, in Florensky’s image?

A god made of wood
Mere decoration with no place in prayer
questions.explanation: The icon is a window. People pray before it because of the person it makes present, not because the panel is divine.

questions.prompt: Which practice does this reading describe?
choices: Praying before icons, kissing them, and treating them as sacred
Worshipping the paint as a second god
Forbidding every image of Christ
questions.explanation: The icon is venerated as holy. That is not the same as worshipping the material as God.

challenges.title: The words themselves: essence, person, nature
challenges.summary: Learn what ousia, hypostasis, and physis mean before using them to explain God and Christ.
challenges.source: Cappadocian Fathers · OCA · The Three Divine Persons

lessons.heading: Start with the question being asked
lessons.body: The Fathers use different words because they are answering different questions. Ousia asks what something is: God is one divine essence. Hypostasis asks who someone is: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Physis means nature, the kind of being and the capacities that belong to it. Keep the questions separate and the terms stay clear.

lessons.heading: A hypostasis is a real who
lessons.body: A hypostasis is a concrete, distinct subject: someone who truly exists and acts. In God there are three Hypostases. They are not parts of God, not competing individuals, and not three separate centers of divinity. The Cappadocians, including Basil of Caesarea, Gregory of Nyssa, and Gregory the Theologian, guarded both the real distinction of the Persons and the unity of God.

lessons.heading: Physis names a nature
lessons.body: Physis and ousia can overlap, so context matters. Speaking of God, one physis means one divine nature. Speaking of Christ, he has two physeis: complete divinity and complete humanity. A nature is not automatically a separate person. Nature answers what kind of life and powers someone has; hypostasis identifies who is acting.

lessons.heading: The word 'God'
lessons.body: The catechism begins with the word itself. Peoples named God out of an encounter, not out of a theory, and the names in their languages still carry that meeting. To Israel God gave the name Yahweh, “The One Who Is”: the One who truly has being. Israel’s refusal to pronounce that Name was not forgetfulness. It was reverence. The lesson to keep is that a person can be at one with God by a trembling silence as truly as by a definition. Say “God” carefully. The word points past every word.

questions.prompt: When you say God has one ousia, what are you talking about?
choices: One Person wearing three temporary masks
The one divine essence shared by Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
Three separate divine beings
questions.explanation: Ousia names what God is. Orthodoxy confesses one undivided divine essence, not three gods and not one Person acting under three temporary masks.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses hypostasis correctly?
choices: God changes from one hypostasis into another
Jesus has two hypostases because he has two natures
The Father is one Hypostasis, and the Son is another distinct Hypostasis
questions.explanation: Father and Son are distinct Hypostases. God does not change from one Person into another, and Christ is not two persons because he has two natures.

questions.prompt: What mistake should you avoid with the word nature?
choices: Saying Christ's humanity is unreal
Treating every nature as automatically a separate person
Using nature to answer what kind of being someone is
questions.explanation: A nature answers the question what, but it does not by itself settle who is acting. That distinction lets the Church confess one Christ with real divine and human natures.

questions.prompt: What does the name Yahweh mean in this reading?
choices: “The One Who Is,” the One who truly has being
“The highest angel,” a creature God promoted
“The world itself,” so that God and creation are the same
questions.explanation: Yahweh is taken as “The One Who Is”: God is the One who truly has being, not a promoted creature and not the world itself.

questions.prompt: Why did Israel refrain from pronouncing the divine Name?
choices: Because God had not yet revealed anything
As reverence: union with God can come through trembling silence, not only through words
Because the Name was considered a magic spell
questions.explanation: The silence is reverent. A person can be at one with God through trembling silence as well as through descriptions.

lessonsEs.heading: Empieza por la pregunta que se está haciendo
lessonsEs.body: Los Padres usan palabras distintas porque responden preguntas distintas. Ousía pregunta qué es algo: Dios es una sola esencia divina. Hipóstasis pregunta quién es alguien: Padre, Hijo y Espíritu Santo. Physis significa naturaleza, el tipo de ser y las capacidades que le pertenecen. Mantén separadas las preguntas y los términos se quedan claros.

No son partes de Dios, ni individuos en competencia, ni tres centros separados de divinidad. Los capadocios, entre ellos Basilio de Cesarea, Gregorio de Nisa y Gregorio el Teólogo, guardaron tanto la distinción real de las Personas como la unidad de Dios.

La naturaleza responde qué tipo de vida y de poderes tiene alguien; la hipóstasis identifica quién está actuando.

lessonsEs.heading: La palabra “Dios”
lessonsEs.body: El catecismo empieza por la palabra misma. Los pueblos nombraron a Dios a partir de un encuentro, no de una teoría, y los nombres en sus lenguas todavía llevan ese encuentro. A Israel Dios le dio el nombre Yahvé, “El que es”: el que de verdad tiene el ser. Que Israel se negara a pronunciar ese Nombre no era olvido. Era reverencia. La lección que hay que guardar es que una persona puede estar unida a Dios por un silencio tembloroso tan de verdad como por una definición. Di “Dios” con cuidado. La palabra señala más allá de toda palabra.

challenges.title: One God in three Hypostases
challenges.summary: Confess homoousios, the Father as source, and perichoresis without falling into modalism, subordinationism, or tritheism.
challenges.source: Athanasius and John of Damascus · OCA · The Holy Trinity

lessons.heading: Homoousios: the Son is truly God
lessons.body: Nicaea calls the Son homoousios with the Father: of the same essence. Athanasius defended this against Arius because a creature, however exalted, could not unite humanity to God or grant divine life. The Son is not a lesser second God; he is truly God from truly God.

lessons.heading: The Father is the source
lessons.body: Orthodoxy speaks of the Father as the one source within the Trinity. The Son is eternally begotten of the Father, and the Holy Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father. Begotten and proceeding describe eternal relations, not events in time. Being from the Father does not make the Son or the Spirit lower in essence, glory, or divinity.

lessons.heading: Perichoresis: communion without confusion
lessons.body: John of Damascus uses perichoresis for the mutual indwelling of the divine Persons. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct, yet they are never separate, divided, or acting as three independent gods. Their unity is not a blur: the Persons remain distinct while sharing one undivided divine life.

lessons.heading: 'Father' as a divine name
lessons.body: “Father” is the Bible’s own name for God. Isaiah 63:16 already puts it on Israel’s lips: “Thou, O Lord, art our Father.” The Eastern tradition keeps masculine names for the Father and the Son because that is how God has named Himself in Scripture, not because God is male in the creaturely sense. There is a difference worth guarding. Biblical anthropomorphism comes from a real meeting with the personal God. It is not the same thing as a modern habit of rebuilding God in the image of our preferences. Call Him Father because He has called Himself Father.

lessons.heading: The mystery of the Trinity
lessons.body: Christians confess one God: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. That is one God in three Hypostases, not three gods and not one person changing masks. Arithmetic will call “one and three” absurd. Faith calls it the cornerstone. The Lord speaks of His unity with the Father and, in the same breath, of being sent by the Father. Distinction and unity arrive together. The Trinity was not a late addition pasted onto a simple monotheism. It lay hidden in the heart of the confession that God is one, until the Son and the Spirit made it known.

questions.prompt: What does homoousios protect?
choices: The Son is the highest creature
The Son is of the same essence as the Father
The Father becomes the Son at the baptism of Jesus
questions.explanation: Homoousios means of the same essence. It rejects Arianism: the Son is not created or lesser in divinity, but truly God together with the Father.

questions.prompt: Which wording keeps the Father as source without subordinationism?
choices: The Son began later and is less divine
The Father is one mode that the Son later replaces
The Son is eternally from the Father and fully God
questions.explanation: The Son is eternally begotten of the Father, so there was never a time when the Son was not. Eternal origin does not mean inferior essence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence avoids both modalism and tritheism?
choices: The three are three independent beings who cooperate
Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct Persons who are never separate gods
Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one Person appearing in three roles
questions.explanation: The first choice divides God into three beings, and the third turns the Persons into roles or masks. Orthodox teaching confesses three distinct Hypostases, one essence, and one undivided divine life.

questions.prompt: Why does the Eastern tradition keep the name Father for God?
choices: Because God is a male creature
Because Father is the biblical name, given in God’s own revelation
Because later philosophy invented it to replace Yahweh
questions.explanation: Father is the traditional biblical name. Isaiah 63:16 already calls the Lord “our Father.”

questions.prompt: What distinguishes biblical anthropomorphism in this reading?
choices: It is based on the experience of the personal God in revelation
It means God has a human body by nature
It is the same as rebuilding God to match modern taste
questions.explanation: Biblical anthropomorphism comes from revelation and encounter. It is not a license to remake God in our image.

questions.prompt: What does “one God in three Hypostases” deny?
choices: That the Father and the Son are distinct
Both three gods and one person wearing three masks
That Jesus was sent by the Father
questions.explanation: The confession keeps one God and three real Hypostases. It refuses tritheism and modalism together.

questions.prompt: Where does this reading locate the Trinity in Israel’s faith?
choices: As a foreign idea with no root in the confession of the one God
Hidden in the heart of the dogma of divine unity, then made known in the Son and the Spirit
As three gods Israel already worshipped by name
questions.explanation: The Trinity is not an extra god beside the God of Israel. It was hidden within the confession of the one God.

lessonsEs.heading: Homoousios: el Hijo es verdaderamente Dios
lessonsEs.body: Nicea llama al Hijo homoousios con el Padre: de la misma esencia. Atanasio defendió esto contra Arrio porque una criatura, por exaltada que fuera, no podía unir la humanidad a Dios ni conceder la vida divina. El Hijo no es un segundo dios menor; es verdaderamente Dios de verdaderamente Dios.
lessonsEs.headingEs: Homoousios: el Hijo es verdaderamente Dios
lessonsEs.bodyEs: Nicea llama al Hijo homoousios con el Padre: de la misma esencia. lessonsEs.heading: El Padre es la fuente
lessonsEs.body: La Ortodoxia habla del Padre como la única fuente dentro de la Trinidad. El Hijo es engendrado eternamente del Padre, y el Espíritu Santo procede eternamente del Padre. Engendrado y procedente describen relaciones eternas, no sucesos en el tiempo. Ser del Padre no hace al Hijo ni al Espíritu inferiores en esencia, gloria o divinidad.

Engendrado y procedente describen relaciones eternas, no sucesos en el tiempo. Ser del Padre no hace al Hijo ni al Espíritu inferiores en esencia, gloria o divinidad.

lessonsEs.heading: Perijóresis: comunión sin confusión
lessonsEs.body: Juan Damasceno usa perijóresis para la inhabitación mutua de las Personas divinas. El Padre, el Hijo y el Espíritu Santo son distintos, y sin embargo nunca están separados, divididos ni actuando como tres dioses independientes. Su unidad no es un borrón: las Personas permanecen distintas mientras comparten una sola vida divina indivisa.

lessonsEs.heading: “Padre” como nombre divino
lessonsEs.body: “Padre” es el nombre que la Biblia misma le da a Dios. Isaías 63:16 ya lo pone en labios de Israel: “tú, oh Jehová, eres nuestro padre”. La tradición oriental conserva los nombres masculinos para el Padre y el Hijo porque así se ha nombrado Dios a sí mismo en la Escritura, no porque Dios sea varón en el sentido de las criaturas. Hay una diferencia que vale la pena guardar. El antropomorfismo bíblico viene de un encuentro real con el Dios personal. No es lo mismo que la costumbre moderna de rehacer a Dios a imagen de nuestras preferencias. Llámalo Padre porque él se ha llamado Padre.

lessonsEs.heading: El misterio de la Trinidad
lessonsEs.body: Los cristianos confiesan un solo Dios: Padre, Hijo y Espíritu Santo. Eso es un solo Dios en tres Hipóstasis, no tres dioses y no una persona que cambia de máscaras. La aritmética llamará absurdo “uno y tres”. La fe lo llama la piedra angular. El Señor habla de su unidad con el Padre y, en el mismo aliento, de ser enviado por el Padre. La distinción y la unidad llegan juntas. La Trinidad no fue un añadido tardío pegado a un monoteísmo simple. Estaba escondida en el corazón de la confesión de que Dios es uno, hasta que el Hijo y el Espíritu la dieron a conocer.

La distinción y la unidad llegan juntas. La Trinidad no fue un añadido tardío pegado a un monoteísmo simple. Estaba escondida en el corazón de la confesión de que Dios es uno, hasta que el Hijo y el Espíritu la dieron a conocer.

challenges.title: Eternal manifestation: from the Father, not from time
challenges.summary: The Son is eternally begotten and the Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father. Eternal manifestation through the Son is not creation and not the temporal sending.
challenges.source: Cappadocian Fathers and the Council of Blachernae · OCA · The Holy Trinity

lessons.heading: Eternal relations are not events
lessons.body: The Son and the Holy Spirit are eternally manifested from the Father. The Son is eternally begotten, and the Spirit eternally proceeds. There was never a time when the Son was not, and never a time when the Spirit was not. Basil the Great, Gregory of Nyssa, and Gregory the Theologian taught these as relations inside the one God, not as episodes on a timeline. John 1:1 says the Word “was” with God. That “was” has no starting day.

lessons.heading: One source, two modes
lessons.body: The Father is the one source within the Trinity, the monarchy. The Son is begotten. The Spirit proceeds. Those are two modes of coming from the Father, not two names for one relation, and not a second begetting of the Spirit. Coming from the Father does not make the Son or the Spirit a lesser essence. Each is fully God, with the Father, before all ages.

lessons.heading: Not creation
lessons.body: John 1:3 says all things were made by the Word, and without him was not anything made that was made. If everything made was made through him, he is not one of the things that were made. Begetting is not making, and procession is not creating. Speak of eternal manifestation as if it were creation, and the speech has already slipped into Arianism: the Son or the Spirit becomes a creature, however high.

lessons.heading: Temporal mission is another grammar
lessons.body: The Father sends the Son when the fullness of time has come (Galatians 4:4). The Spirit is sent at Pentecost. John 1:1 names the Word who already was God. John 1:14 names the Word made flesh: that is the mission in time. John 15:26 holds both grammars in one verse: “which proceedeth from the Father” is the eternal relation, and “whom I will send” is the mission. The sending reveals the relation. It does not begin it. Mission asks when he came to us. Origin asks from whom he is, eternally.

lessons.heading: Manifested through the Son, not a second source
lessons.body: The Council of Blachernae in 1285, following Gregory of Cyprus, confessed that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father alone and is eternally manifested through the Son. The Spirit shines forth and rests in the Son. That shining is not a second birth, and it does not make the Son a cause of the Spirit’s person. The Filioque names the Son as a cause of that person. This confession does not. St Gregory Palamas keeps a further line: what God manifests to creatures is uncreated energy, not the Spirit’s hypostasis. The same fence is the one kept in this catechesis. Eternal manifestation through the Son is not a second source, and it is not the sending in time.

questions.prompt: What does “eternally begotten” deny?
choices: That the Son is truly God

questions.explanation: Eternal begetting means there was never a time when the Son was not. It is a relation in God, not an event on a timeline.

questions.prompt: As to his person, from whom does the Holy Spirit proceed?

questions.prompt: What is eternal manifestation through the Son?

questions.explanation: Blachernae and Gregory of Cyprus distinguish procession from the Father alone from eternal manifestation through the Son. Manifestation is not a second cause, and it is not only the day of Pentecost.

questions.prompt: What is Pentecost in this grammar?
choices: The moment the Spirit began to exist

questions.explanation: Pentecost is the Spirit’s mission in time. The Spirit already proceeds eternally from the Father.

questions.prompt: Why must the Son’s origin not be called creation?

questions.explanation: If everything made was made through him, he is not one of the things made. Confusing manifestation with creation is the Arian slide.

lessonsEs.heading: Las relaciones eternas no son sucesos
lessonsEs.body: El Hijo y el Espíritu Santo se manifiestan eternamente desde el Padre. El Hijo es engendrado eternamente, y el Espíritu procede eternamente. Nunca hubo un tiempo en que el Hijo no fuera, ni un tiempo en que el Espíritu no fuera. Basilio el Grande, Gregorio de Nisa y Gregorio el Teólogo enseñaron esto como relaciones dentro del único Dios, no como episodios en una línea de tiempo. Juan 1:1 dice que el Verbo «era» con Dios: «En el principio era el Verbo, y el Verbo era con Dios, y el Verbo era Dios» (Juan 1:1, RV1909). Ese «era» no tiene día de comienzo.

Basilio el Grande, Gregorio de Nisa y Gregorio el Teólogo enseñaron esto como relaciones dentro del único Dios, no como episodios en una línea de tiempo. lessonsEs.heading: Una fuente, dos modos
lessonsEs.body: El Padre es la única fuente dentro de la Trinidad: la monarquía. El Hijo es engendrado. El Espíritu procede. Son dos modos de venir del Padre, no dos nombres para una sola relación, y no un segundo engendramiento del Espíritu. Venir del Padre no vuelve al Hijo ni al Espíritu una esencia menor. Cada uno es plenamente Dios, con el Padre, antes de todos los siglos.

Cada uno es plenamente Dios, con el Padre, antes de todos los siglos.

lessonsEs.heading: No es creación
lessonsEs.body: Juan 1:3 dice que todas las cosas fueron hechas por el Verbo, y que sin él nada de lo que fue hecho llegó a ser: «Todas las cosas por él fueron hechas; y sin él nada de lo que es hecho, fué hecho» (Juan 1:3, RV1909). Si todo lo hecho fue hecho por medio de él, él no es una de las cosas que fueron hechas. Engendrar no es fabricar, y proceder no es crear. Si hablas de la manifestación eterna como si fuera creación, tu palabra ya se deslizó al arrianismo: el Hijo o el Espíritu se vuelve criatura, por muy alto que lo pongas.

Si todo lo hecho fue hecho por medio de él, él no es una de las cosas que fueron hechas. Engendrar no es fabricar, y proceder no es crear. Si hablas de la manifestación eterna como si fuera creación, tu palabra ya se deslizó al arrianismo: el Hijo o el Espíritu se vuelve criatura, por muy alto que lo pongas.

lessonsEs.heading: La misión en el tiempo es otra gramática
lessonsEs.body: El Padre envía al Hijo cuando llega el cumplimiento del tiempo: «Mas venido el cumplimiento del tiempo, Dios envió su Hijo, hecho de mujer, hecho súbdito á la ley» (Gálatas 4:4, RV1909). El Espíritu es enviado en Pentecostés. Juan 1:1 nombra al Verbo que ya era Dios. Juan 1:14 nombra al Verbo hecho carne: «Y aquel Verbo fué hecho carne, y habitó entre nosotros» (Juan 1:14, RV1909). Esa es la misión en el tiempo. Juan 15:26 sostiene las dos gramáticas en un solo versículo: «el cual procede del Padre» es la relación eterna, y «el cual yo os enviaré» es la misión (Juan 15:26, RV1909). El envío revela la relación. No la comienza. La misión pregunta cuándo vino a nosotros. El origen pregunta de quién es, eternamente.

El Espíritu es enviado en Pentecostés. Juan 1:1 nombra al Verbo que ya era Dios. Juan 1:14 nombra al Verbo hecho carne: «Y aquel Verbo fué hecho carne, y habitó entre nosotros» (Juan 1:14, RV1909). lessonsEs.heading: Manifestado por el Hijo, no una segunda fuente
lessonsEs.body: El Concilio de Blaquernas, en 1285, siguiendo a Gregorio de Chipre, confesó que el Espíritu Santo procede solo del Padre y es manifestado eternamente por el Hijo. El Espíritu resplandece y descansa en el Hijo. Ese resplandor no es un segundo nacimiento, y no hace del Hijo una causa de la persona del Espíritu. El Filioque nombra al Hijo como causa de esa persona. Esta confesión no lo hace. San Gregorio Palamás guarda una línea más: lo que Dios manifiesta a las criaturas es energía increada, no la hipóstasis del Espíritu. La misma cerca es la que guarda esta catequesis. La manifestación eterna por el Hijo no es una segunda fuente, y no es el envío en el tiempo.

challenges.title: Speaking About the Godhead Without Heresy
challenges.level: 5 teaching cards · 10 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: How to speak about Father, Son, and Holy Spirit without making the essence a fourth thing. The persons are the who; the essence is the what. Relations of origin distinguish the persons; they never divide the one essence.
challenges.source: Deuteronomy 6:4 · Isaiah 44:6 · Matthew 28:19 · John 1:1 · John 8:42 · John 15:26 · John 20:28

lessons.heading: Not a fourth thing
lessons.body: Begin with the mistake this lesson exists to prevent. When we say Father, Son, and Holy Spirit share one divine essence, the essence is not a fourth item standing behind them: not a container they sit inside, not a committee member, not a lump of God-stuff divided three ways. The essence is simply what God is. The persons are who God is. Say the formula until it steadies your speech: the persons are the who; the essence is the what. Three persons, one essence — not four things.

lessons.heading: The essence is not a subject
lessons.body: A subject acts, wills, speaks, and loves. The divine essence, as such, does none of those things apart from the persons. We never pray to the essence; we pray to the Father, through the Son, in the Holy Spirit. God acts personally: the Father sends, the Son becomes flesh, the Spirit sanctifies — each according to the one undivided divine nature. This protects the faith both ways. It stops us inventing a nameless fourth god behind the Trinity, and it stops us shrinking the persons into masks, because real subjects are the ones who act.

lessons.heading: Distinguished by origin, not by pieces
lessons.body: What distinguishes the persons is not parts of the essence, rank, or size. It is relations of origin. The Father is unbegotten: he is the source without origin. The Son is begotten: eternally from the Father, not made. The Spirit proceeds: eternally from the Father. Those relations do not slice the essence; each person is fully God, possessing the whole divine nature, not a third of it. Origin tells us who is who. It never turns one God into three gods, and it never makes the Son or Spirit lesser gods.

lessons.heading: Say it clean
lessons.body: Use the grammar this lesson trains. You may say: one God, because one essence; three persons, because Father, Son, and Spirit are really distinct; the Son is God, the Spirit is God, and the Father is God — each fully, not partly. Do not say: the essence decided, the Godhead as a fourth being acted, the Son is one third of God, or the persons are three roles. Carry the same grammar into Christology: in the hypostatic union the same who/what distinction keeps you from splitting Christ or mixing his natures. First fix the subject, then speak.

lessons.heading: Unity of love
lessons.body: The Trinity is not a frozen object. In God there is the fullness of life and of love. “God is love” (1 John 4:8) cannot mean a lonely monad, because love has no beloved if there is no other. The Persons give and receive: the Son has all that the Father has, and the Spirit takes what is the Son’s and declares it (John 16:15). St Philaret of Moscow named the Cross in a Trinitarian way: the crucifying love of the Father, the crucified love of the Son, and the love of the Holy Spirit triumphing by the power of the Cross. Speak of one essence without turning God into a solitary will that has no one to love.

questions.prompt: If the divine essence is not a fourth thing, what is it?
choices: A container that holds the three persons
The one what that Father, Son, and Spirit fully share
A fourth member of the Trinity
A quantity of divine material divided into thirds
questions.explanation: The persons are the who; the essence is the what. One essence, three persons — not four things.

questions.prompt: The formula “the persons are the who, the essence is the what” mainly guards against...
choices: Saying anything about God at all
Turning the essence into a separate subject behind the persons
Calling the Son God
Distinguishing Father, Son, and Spirit
questions.explanation: The essence names what God is; the persons are the real subjects who act, will, and love.

questions.prompt: True or false: the divine essence acts and wills by itself apart from the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: False. The essence is not a subject. The persons act according to the one divine nature.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit?
choices: Each owns a different third of the essence
Relations of origin: the Father is unbegotten, the Son is begotten, the Spirit proceeds
The Father is more God than the Son and Spirit
They are three temporary roles
questions.explanation: Relations of origin distinguish the persons within the one essence; they do not divide it or rank it.

questions.prompt: True or false: each person is fully God, not one third of God.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: True. The essence is undivided. Each person possesses the whole divine nature.

questions.prompt: A friend says, “The Godhead decided to send Jesus,” as if the Godhead were a fourth actor behind the Father. What is the cleaner statement?
choices: The essence sent the Son
The Father sent the Son in the Holy Spirit
The Godhead voted and the Son obeyed
No one sent him; sending is only a metaphor
questions.explanation: Sending is personal action: the Father sends, the Son is sent, the Spirit is given. The essence is not a fourth actor.

questions.prompt: Why do relations of origin not divide the essence?
choices: Because origin is only about time, not eternity
Because begotten and proceeding name who each person is, not pieces or amounts of what God is
Because the Son and Spirit are not fully God
Because essence and person are the same word
questions.explanation: Origin distinguishes the who. It does not cut the what into parts.

questions.prompt: True or false: “Three persons, one essence” means three gods who agree with each other.
choices: True

lessonsEs.heading: No es una cuarta cosa
lessonsEs.body: Empieza por el error que esta lección existe para impedir. Cuando decimos que el Padre, el Hijo y el Espíritu Santo comparten una sola esencia divina, la esencia no es un cuarto objeto puesto detrás de ellos: no es un recipiente en el que se sientan, no es un miembro de un comité, no es un trozo de «materia divina» repartido en tres partes. La esencia es simplemente lo que Dios es. Las personas son quién es Dios. Repite la fórmula hasta que te afirme el habla: las personas son el quién; la esencia es el qué. Tres personas, una esencia: no cuatro cosas.

lessonsEs.heading: La esencia no es un sujeto
lessonsEs.body: Un sujeto actúa, quiere, habla y ama. La esencia divina, como tal, no hace ninguna de esas cosas aparte de las personas. Nunca oramos a la esencia; oramos al Padre, por el Hijo, en el Espíritu Santo. Dios actúa de modo personal: el Padre envía, el Hijo se hace carne, el Espíritu santifica, cada uno según la única naturaleza divina indivisa. Esto protege la fe por los dos lados. Te impide inventar un cuarto dios sin nombre detrás de la Trinidad, y te impide encoger a las personas hasta volverlas máscaras, porque los sujetos reales son los que actúan.

lessonsEs.heading: Se distinguen por el origen, no por pedazos
lessonsEs.body: Lo que distingue a las personas no son partes de la esencia, ni el rango, ni el tamaño. Son las relaciones de origen. El Padre es ingénito: es la fuente sin origen. El Hijo es engendrado: eternamente del Padre, no hecho. El Espíritu procede: eternamente del Padre. Esas relaciones no parten la esencia; cada persona es plenamente Dios y posee toda la naturaleza divina, no un tercio de ella. El origen te dice quién es quién. Nunca convierte al único Dios en tres dioses, y nunca vuelve al Hijo o al Espíritu dioses menores.

lessonsEs.heading: Dilo con limpieza
lessonsEs.body: Usa la gramática que esta lección entrena. Puedes decir: un solo Dios, porque hay una sola esencia; tres personas, porque el Padre, el Hijo y el Espíritu son realmente distintos; el Hijo es Dios, el Espíritu es Dios y el Padre es Dios, cada uno plenamente, no en parte. No digas: la esencia decidió, la Deidad actuó como un cuarto ser, el Hijo es un tercio de Dios, o las personas son tres papeles. Lleva la misma gramática a la cristología: en la unión hipostática, la misma distinción entre quién y qué te guarda de partir a Cristo o de mezclar sus naturalezas. Primero fija el sujeto, y después habla.

lessonsEs.heading: Unidad de amor
lessonsEs.body: La Trinidad no es un objeto congelado. En Dios está la plenitud de la vida y del amor. «Dios es amor» (1 Juan 4:8, RV1909) no puede significar una mónada solitaria, porque el amor no tiene amado si no hay otro. Las Personas dan y reciben: el Hijo tiene todo lo que el Padre tiene, y el Espíritu toma lo que es del Hijo y lo da a conocer: «Todo lo que tiene el Padre, mío es: por eso dije que tomará de lo mío, y os lo hará saber» (Juan 16:15, RV1909). San Filareto de Moscú nombró la Cruz de un modo trinitario: el amor crucificador del Padre, el amor crucificado del Hijo, y el amor del Espíritu Santo que triunfa por el poder de la Cruz. Habla de una sola esencia sin convertir a Dios en una voluntad solitaria que no tiene a quién amar.

challenges.title: The hypostatic union: one Christ, two natures
challenges.summary: Use Chalcedon's guardrails to confess one hypostasis of God the Word in complete divinity and complete humanity.
challenges.source: Cyril of Alexandria and Chalcedon · OCA · Fifth Century

lessons.heading: One who, two whats
lessons.body: In the Incarnation, the one hypostasis of God the Word becomes man without ceasing to be God. He does not join himself to a separate human person. From the Theotokos he assumes complete human nature, including a real body and a rational human soul, and makes that humanity his own.

lessons.heading: Chalcedon's four guardrails
lessons.body: Chalcedon confesses Christ in two natures asynchytos, without confusion; atreptos, without change; adiairetos, without division; and achoristos, without separation. These are fences around the mystery. The natures are not blended into a hybrid, divinity is not altered, Christ is not split into two sons, and the union is not temporary or loose.

lessons.heading: Complete humanity, complete divinity
lessons.body: Cyril of Alexandria guards the unity of Christ, while Maximus the Confessor and the later councils guard his complete humanity. Christ has a real rational human mind and will; his humanity is not swallowed by divinity. He is not a divine appearance, not a body animated directly by divinity instead of a human soul, and not a mixture that leaves him neither fully God nor fully man.

lessons.heading: The Christ of faith: one Person in two natures
lessons.body: The Gospels already show a Christ who is divine and human. The Church still had to say how that is one Lord and not two. From the fourth century to the seventh, the arguments were about that “how.” The faith that emerged is not a new Christ. It is a guard around the Christ of the Gospels: one Person, the Son of God, in two complete natures. When a formula makes Him less than God or less than man, it has left the portrait the Gospels actually draw.

questions.prompt: What does asynchytos, without confusion, rule out?

questions.explanation: Asynchytos rejects the Eutychian confusion of the natures. Christ remains fully God and fully man; the union does not blend divinity and humanity into something else.

questions.prompt: Which claim avoids both Apollinarianism and Eutychianism?
choices: His divinity replaces his human mind, and his humanity is absorbed

questions.explanation: Apollinarianism removes Christ's rational human mind, Eutychianism absorbs or confuses his humanity, and Docetism makes his embodied life only an appearance. The third sentence keeps his humanity complete and real.

questions.prompt: What task did church Tradition face after the Gospels?
choices: To invent a Christ the Gospels do not know
To say how divinity and humanity are one Lord, not two Christs
To deny that Jesus was human
questions.explanation: The dogma guards the Gospel portrait: one Person in two natures, forged through the Christological debates of the fourth to the seventh century.

questions.prompt: When has a Christological formula left the Gospels, in this reading?

When it says He was born
When it uses the word nature at all
questions.explanation: The formulas exist to keep Him fully God and fully man, one Lord. A formula that shrinks either nature has left the text.

lessonsEs.heading: Un quién, dos qués
lessonsEs.body: En la Encarnación, la única hipóstasis de Dios el Verbo se hace hombre sin dejar de ser Dios. No se une a una persona humana aparte. De la Theotokos asume la naturaleza humana completa, con un cuerpo real y un alma humana racional, y hace suya esa humanidad.

lessonsEs.heading: Las cuatro cercas de Calcedonia
lessonsEs.body: Calcedonia confiesa a Cristo en dos naturalezas asynchytos, sin confusión; atreptos, sin cambio; adiairetos, sin división; y achoristos, sin separación. Son cercas alrededor del misterio. Las naturalezas no se mezclan en un híbrido, la divinidad no se altera, Cristo no se parte en dos hijos, y la unión no es pasajera ni floja.

lessonsEs.heading: Humanidad completa, divinidad completa
lessonsEs.body: Cirilo de Alejandría guarda la unidad de Cristo, mientras que Máximo el Confesor y los concilios posteriores guardan su humanidad completa. Cristo tiene una mente humana racional y una voluntad humana reales; su humanidad no es tragada por la divinidad. No es una apariencia divina, no es un cuerpo animado directamente por la divinidad en lugar de un alma humana, y no es una mezcla que lo deje ni plenamente Dios ni plenamente hombre.

lessonsEs.heading: El Cristo de la fe: una Persona en dos naturalezas
lessonsEs.body: Los Evangelios ya muestran a un Cristo que es divino y humano. La Iglesia tuvo que decir todavía cómo ese Señor es uno y no dos. Del siglo cuarto al séptimo, las discusiones fueron sobre ese «cómo». La fe que surgió no es un Cristo nuevo. Es una guarda alrededor del Cristo de los Evangelios: una Persona, el Hijo de Dios, en dos naturalezas completas. Cuando una fórmula lo hace menos que Dios o menos que hombre, ha dejado el retrato que los Evangelios realmente dibujan.

lessons.heading: Theotokos protects who was born
lessons.body: The Church calls Mary Theotokos, Birth-giver of God, because the child she bore is personally God the Word made flesh. The title does not mean Mary created the divine nature or existed before God. It safeguards the unity of Christ: the same Son who is eternally begotten of the Father is born of Mary in the flesh.

lessons.heading: Speak of one subject, carefully
lessons.body: Communicatio idiomatum means that, because Christ is one subject, we may predicate human experiences of God the Word according to the flesh and divine works of the man Jesus according to his divinity. It does not transfer properties between the natures. When we say God suffered in the flesh, we mean the divine Person truly suffered in his human nature; the divine nature did not become passible by nature.

lessons.heading: Keep the same Jesus in every sentence
lessons.body: The same Lord hungers and feeds the multitude, prays and forgives sins, dies and rises. Do not assign the human actions to a separate man and the divine actions to a separate God beside him. Maximus the Confessor and John of Damascus keep both truths together: one incarnate Son acting in complete divinity and complete humanity.

questions.prompt: Why does the Church call Mary Theotokos?
choices: Because Mary is the source of Christ's divinity
Because Mary became a fourth divine Person
Because the child born of her is personally God the Son made man
questions.explanation: Theotokos is first a claim about Christ. Mary did not create the divine nature; she truly gave birth, in the flesh, to the eternal Son who made that humanity his own.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses communicatio idiomatum carefully?
choices: The divine nature changed into passible flesh
God the Word suffered in the flesh, while the divine nature did not become passible by nature
Only a separate human person suffered, not the Son
questions.explanation: Because the sufferer is personally God the Word, Scripture can say the Lord of glory was crucified. The suffering is real in the flesh; the divine nature is not changed into a passible nature.

questions.prompt: Pick the orthodox sentence.
choices: Jesus is a human person inspired by a separate divine Person
Christ is a mixture, neither fully God nor fully man
The same Jesus Christ is fully God and fully man, one Person acting in both natures
questions.explanation: The first sentence divides Christ into two persons, and the second confuses the natures into a mixture. The third keeps one subject and confesses complete divinity and complete humanity.

lessonsEs.heading: Theotokos protege quién nació
lessonsEs.body: La Iglesia llama a María Theotokos, la que dio a luz a Dios, porque el niño que dio a luz es personalmente Dios el Verbo hecho carne. El título no significa que María creó la naturaleza divina ni que existió antes que Dios. Resguarda la unidad de Cristo: el mismo Hijo que es engendrado eternamente del Padre nace de María en la carne.

lessonsEs.heading: Habla de un solo sujeto, con cuidado
lessonsEs.body: Communicatio idiomatum significa que, porque Cristo es un solo sujeto, podemos predicar las experiencias humanas de Dios el Verbo según la carne, y las obras divinas del hombre Jesús según su divinidad. No transfiere las propiedades de una naturaleza a la otra. Cuando decimos que Dios padeció en la carne, queremos decir que la Persona divina padeció de verdad en su naturaleza humana; la naturaleza divina no se volvió pasible por naturaleza.

lessonsEs.heading: Guarda al mismo Jesús en cada frase
lessonsEs.body: El mismo Señor tiene hambre y alimenta a la multitud, ora y perdona pecados, muere y resucita. No asignes las acciones humanas a un hombre aparte y las acciones divinas a un Dios separado junto a él. Máximo el Confesor y Juan Damasceno guardan juntas las dos verdades: un solo Hijo encarnado que actúa en divinidad completa y en humanidad completa.

challenges.title: Asking the saints to pray for us
challenges.level: 3 teaching cards · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: A biblical defense of asking the departed saints for intercession without turning prayer into worship or necromancy.
challenges.source: Revelation 5:8; 8:3-4 · Hebrews 12:1 · 1 Timothy 2:1-5 · the early Church

lessons.heading: The departed saints are alive in Christ
lessons.body: The defense begins with life, not with death. Christ says God is not the God of the dead, but of the living (Luke 20:37-38). Hebrews places us before a great cloud of witnesses (Hebrews 12:1), and Revelation shows the martyrs conscious before God, crying out for justice (Revelation 6:9-10). If the saints live in Christ, asking them to pray is not trying to reach people who vanished; it is asking living members of Christ's body to do what living Christians are told to do.

lessons.heading: Scripture commands intercession and pictures it in heaven
lessons.body: Paul commands that intercessions be made for all people (1 Timothy 2:1-3), and James says the prayer of a righteous person has great power (James 5:16). Revelation gives the same pattern a heavenly picture: the elders hold golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints (Revelation 5:8), and an angel offers incense with the prayers of all the saints before the throne (Revelation 8:3-4). Asking a saint to pray is not a new kind of religion; it is intercession received inside the communion of Christ.

lessons.heading: Not worship, and not necromancy
lessons.body: Orthodox teaching keeps the line clean: worship, latreia, belongs to God alone. Honor toward the saints, often called dulia, is the honor given to God's friends and members of Christ. Necromancy seeks hidden knowledge or control from the dead; the Church asks the saints for prayer to God. Christ remains the one mediator between God and man by nature (1 Timothy 2:5), while His members share in intercession by grace, just as they do on earth.

questions.prompt: In Revelation 5:8, the incense in the golden bowls is identified as what?
choices: The praises of angels only
The prayers of the saints
The smoke of the temple altar
The merits of the apostles
questions.explanation: Revelation 5:8 calls the incense the prayers of the saints. That image gives a biblical frame for heavenly intercession.

questions.prompt: What is the clean distinction when Orthodox Christians ask a saint to pray?
choices: Saints receive latreia because they are lesser gods
The saint replaces Christ as mediator by nature
We ask a living member of Christ to intercede, while worship belongs to God alone
The dead are contacted for secret information
questions.explanation: Asking for intercession is not worship and not necromancy. Christ alone is mediator by nature; His members intercede by grace.

questions.prompt: Why does 1 Timothy 2:5 not cancel 1 Timothy 2:1?
choices: Because Paul commands intercessions in the same passage where he names Christ the one mediator
Because mediator means only an earthly priest
Because saints are mediators by nature too
Because prayer to God is optional after baptism
questions.explanation: Paul's own order matters: intercessions are commanded first, then Christ is confessed as the one mediator. Shared prayer does not compete with His unique mediation.

lessonsEs.heading: Los santos difuntos están vivos en Cristo
lessonsEs.body: La defensa empieza por la vida, no por la muerte. Cristo dice que Dios no es Dios de muertos, sino de vivos: «Porque Dios no es Dios de muertos, mas de vivos: porque todos viven á él» (Lucas 20:38, RV1909; véase 20:37-38). Hebreos nos pone delante de una gran nube de testigos: «teniendo en derredor nuestro una tan grande nube de testigos» (Hebreos 12:1, RV1909). El Apocalipsis muestra a los mártires conscientes delante de Dios, clamando por justicia (Apocalipsis 6:9-10). Si los santos viven en Cristo, pedirles que oren no es intentar alcanzar a gente que desapareció; es pedir a miembros vivos del cuerpo de Cristo que hagan lo que se les manda hacer a los cristianos vivos.

lessonsEs.heading: La Escritura manda la intercesión y la muestra en el cielo
lessonsEs.body: Pablo manda que se hagan intercesiones por todos: «AMONESTO pues, ante todas cosas, que se hagan rogativas, oraciones, peticiones, hacimientos de gracias, por todos los hombres» (1 Timoteo 2:1-3, RV1909). Santiago dice que la oración del justo puede mucho: «la oración del justo, obrando eficazmente, puede mucho» (Santiago 5:16, RV1909). El Apocalipsis le da a ese mismo patrón una imagen celestial: los ancianos tienen copas de oro llenas de incienso, que son las oraciones de los santos (Apocalipsis 5:8), y un ángel ofrece incienso con las oraciones de todos los santos delante del trono (Apocalipsis 8:3-4). Pedirle a un santo que ore no es una religión nueva; es intercesión recibida dentro de la comunión de Cristo.

lessonsEs.heading: No es adoración, ni necromancia
lessonsEs.body: La enseñanza ortodoxa guarda la línea limpia: la adoración, la latría, pertenece solo a Dios. El honor hacia los santos, a menudo llamado dulía, es el honor dado a los amigos de Dios y a los miembros de Cristo. La necromancia busca conocimiento oculto o control de parte de los muertos; la Iglesia pide a los santos oración a Dios. Cristo sigue siendo el único mediador entre Dios y los hombres por naturaleza: «Porque hay un Dios, asimismo un mediador entre Dios y los hombres, Jesucristo hombre» (1 Timoteo 2:5, RV1909). Sus miembros participan de la intercesión por gracia, igual que lo hacen en la tierra.

questionsEs.explanation: Pedir intercesión no es adoración ni necromancia. Solo Cristo es mediador por naturaleza; sus miembros interceden por gracia.

challenges.title: Calling Mary Theotokos
challenges.summary: Why God-bearer is first a confession about Jesus: the child born of Mary is truly God the Word made flesh.
challenges.source: Luke 1:43 · John 1:1-14 · Galatians 4:4 · St. Cyril of Alexandria and Ephesus, 431

lessons.heading: Elizabeth already calls her the mother of my Lord
lessons.body: When Mary visits Elizabeth, Elizabeth cries out, why is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? (Luke 1:43). In that setting, Lord is not a polite title for a merely human baby. The question is not first about Mary. It is about who the child is. If the child in her womb is the Lord, then Mary is rightly named by relation to Him.

lessons.heading: The Word became flesh; the Son was born of a woman
lessons.body: John confesses that the Word was God and that the Word became flesh (John 1:1, 14). Paul says God sent forth his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). The Church does not say Mary created the divine nature. She bore, according to the flesh, the one Person who is God the Son. The word Theotokos means God-bearer; it guards the unity of Jesus Christ against splitting Him into God over here and a separate man over there.

lessons.heading: Ephesus protected Christ, not a rivalry with Him
lessons.body: At Ephesus in 431, St. Cyril of Alexandria defended Theotokos because denying it threatened the confession that Emmanuel is truly God. The title does not make Mary the source of the Trinity. It says that the same Son who is eternally begotten of the Father was truly born of Mary in time. Keep the phrase according to the flesh close by: Mary is mother of God incarnate, not mother of divinity as an abstract nature.

lessons.heading: The Mother of God and the saints
lessons.body: The Church’s honor of women is shown first in the place she gives the Mother of God: higher than the saints, higher than the angels, “more honorable than the cherubim and beyond compare more glorious than the seraphim.” That glory is Christ’s. The saints are not a crowd of independent patrons. They are bound to Christ and therefore to one another. A Christian community that has no living communion with them does not yet know the Church as the whole mystical Body, the living and the departed in one Christ. Ask the saints to pray because they are alive in Him. Do not give them the worship that belongs to God alone.

questions.prompt: What does Elizabeth call Mary in Luke 1:43?
choices: The mother of my Lord
The queen above the Trinity
The mother of a prophet only
The source of the divine nature
questions.explanation: Luke 1:43 gives the biblical seed of the title: mother of my Lord. The title follows from the identity of the child.

questions.prompt: What danger does the title Theotokos guard against?
choices: Saying Jesus had a real mother
Splitting Christ into a separate God and a separate man loosely joined together
Calling Mary blessed among women
Confessing that Christ was born in Bethlehem
questions.explanation: Theotokos protects the one Person of Christ. It refuses a Jesus who is partly attached to God from outside.

questions.prompt: What does Theotokos not mean?
choices: Mary bore God the Word according to the flesh
Jesus is truly God and truly man
Mary is the origin or creator of the divine nature
Elizabeth spoke by the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Mary did not create divinity. She bore the divine Son in His incarnation, so the title confesses Christ without exaggerating Mary into a source of Godhead.

questions.prompt: Where does this reading place the Mother of God?
choices: Above the saints and the angels, because of the Child she bore
As a fourth Person of the Trinity
As an ordinary believer the Church does not single out
questions.explanation: She is glorified above saints and angels. The glory is about Christ, whose mother she is.

questions.prompt: What is missing where the saints are not in living communion with the Church?
choices: Nothing; the Body of Christ is only the people in one building
The fullness of the Church as the one Body joining the living and the departed in Christ
The right to worship the saints as God
questions.explanation: The saints belong to the Church’s fullness. Communion with them is not worship of them as God.

lessonsEs.heading: Elisabet ya la llama la madre de mi Señor
lessonsEs.body: Cuando María visita a Elisabet, Elisabet exclama: «¿Y de dónde esto á mí, que la madre de mi Señor venga á mí?» (Lucas 1:43, RV1909). En ese escenario, Señor no es un título cortés para un bebé meramente humano. La pregunta no es primero acerca de María. Es acerca de quién es el niño. Si el niño en su vientre es el Señor, entonces María es nombrada con razón por su relación con él.

lessonsEs.heading: El Verbo se hizo carne; el Hijo nació de mujer
lessonsEs.body: Juan confiesa que el Verbo era Dios y que el Verbo se hizo carne (Juan 1:1, 14): «el Verbo era Dios» y «aquel Verbo fué hecho carne» (RV1909). Pablo dice que Dios envió a su Hijo, hecho de mujer (Gálatas 4:4). La Iglesia no dice que María creó la naturaleza divina. Ella dio a luz, según la carne, a la única Persona que es Dios el Hijo. La palabra Theotokos significa la que dio a luz a Dios; guarda la unidad de Jesucristo contra partirlo en un Dios por un lado y un hombre aparte por el otro.

lessonsEs.heading: Éfeso protegió a Cristo, no una rivalidad con él
lessonsEs.body: En Éfeso, en el año 431, san Cirilo de Alejandría defendió el título Theotokos porque negarlo amenazaba la confesión de que Emanuel es verdaderamente Dios. El título no hace de María la fuente de la Trinidad. Dice que el mismo Hijo que es engendrado eternamente del Padre nació de verdad de María en el tiempo. Ten cerca la frase «según la carne»: María es madre de Dios encarnado, no madre de la divinidad como naturaleza abstracta.

lessonsEs.heading: La Madre de Dios y los santos
lessonsEs.body: El honor que la Iglesia da a las mujeres se muestra primero en el lugar que le da a la Madre de Dios: más alta que los santos, más alta que los ángeles, «más honorable que los querubines e incomparablemente más gloriosa que los serafines». Esa gloria es de Cristo. Los santos no son una multitud de patronos independientes. Están unidos a Cristo y, por eso, unos a otros. Una comunidad cristiana que no tiene comunión viva con ellos todavía no conoce a la Iglesia como el Cuerpo místico entero, los vivos y los difuntos en un solo Cristo. Pide a los santos que oren porque están vivos en él. No les des la adoración que pertenece solo a Dios.

Una comunidad cristiana que no tiene comunión viva con ellos todavía no conoce a la Iglesia como el Cuerpo místico entero, los vivos y los difuntos en un solo Cristo. Pide a los santos que oren porque están vivos en él. No les des la adoración que pertenece solo a Dios.

challenges.title: The true Body and Blood
challenges.summary: Why Orthodox Christians receive the Eucharist as real communion in Christ's Body and Blood, not as a bare reminder.
challenges.source: Matthew 26:26-28 · John 6:53-56 · 1 Corinthians 10:16; 11:23-29 · St. Ignatius of Antioch

lessons.heading: Take the words of institution at full weight
lessons.body: At the Mystical Supper Christ does not say, this only pictures my body. He says, This is my body, and, This is my blood of the new covenant (Matthew 26:26-28). Paul hands on the same words as a received tradition and warns the Corinthians to examine themselves and discern the body (1 Corinthians 11:23-29). A defense can be simple: the Church believes the Eucharist is what Christ calls it, received by faith in the mystery He gives.

lessons.heading: John 6 and the language of participation
lessons.body: In John 6 Christ says His flesh is true food and His blood is true drink, and that the one who eats and drinks abides in Him. Paul uses the word koinonia for the cup and the bread: a participation or communion in the blood and body of Christ (1 Corinthians 10:16). That is stronger than a mental reminder. Communion joins the faithful to Christ and to one another in His body.

lessons.heading: Real, sacramental, and approached with fear and faith
lessons.body: Orthodox teaching does not reduce the mystery to a laboratory object, and it does not turn the Eucharist into crude cannibalism. The gifts are truly the Body and Blood of Christ by the action of the Holy Spirit, received sacramentally under the forms of bread and wine. St. Ignatius of Antioch already called the Eucharist the medicine of immortality. Because the gift is real, Paul joins communion to repentance, reconciliation, and discernment.

questions.prompt: In 1 Corinthians 10:16, Paul calls the cup and bread a participation in what?
choices: A church picnic and a memory aid
The blood and body of Christ
The opinions of the Corinthians
A symbol with no gift given
questions.explanation: Paul's word is koinonia: participation or communion. The cup is participation in the blood of Christ; the bread is participation in the body of Christ.

questions.prompt: Which words of Christ stand behind the Orthodox defense?
choices: This represents my body from a distance
This is my body; this is my blood
This is only a teaching illustration
Do this until symbols are no longer useful
questions.explanation: The institution words are the anchor: This is my body, and, This is my blood. Orthodoxy receives them as gift and mystery, not as a bare sign.

questions.prompt: What does a reverent defense avoid claiming?
choices: That communion is a real participation in Christ
That the Eucharist is a crude physical object lesson rather than a sacramental mystery
That believers should examine themselves before communion
That John 6 speaks of eating and drinking
questions.explanation: The defense is real but not crude. Orthodoxy confesses the true Body and Blood while receiving the mystery sacramentally, with repentance and faith.

lessonsEs.heading: Toma las palabras de la institución con todo su peso
lessonsEs.body: En la Cena Mística, Cristo no dice: esto solo representa mi cuerpo. Dice: «esto es mi cuerpo», y «esto es mi sangre del nuevo pacto» (Mateo 26:26-28, RV1909). Pablo entrega las mismas palabras como una tradición recibida y advierte a los corintios que se prueben a sí mismos y disciernan el cuerpo (1 Corintios 11:23-29). Una defensa puede ser sencilla: la Iglesia cree que la Eucaristía es lo que Cristo dice que es, recibida por la fe en el misterio que él da.

lessonsEs.heading: Juan 6 y el lenguaje de la participación
lessonsEs.body: En Juan 6, Cristo dice que su carne es verdadera comida y su sangre es verdadera bebida, y que quien come y bebe permanece en él: «Porque mi carne es verdadera comida, y mi sangre es verdadera bebida. El que come mi carne y bebe mi sangre, en mí permanece, y yo en él» (Juan 6:55-56, RV1909). Pablo usa la palabra koinonía para la copa y el pan: una participación o comunión en la sangre y el cuerpo de Cristo. «La copa de bendición que bendecimos, ¿no es la comunión de la sangre de Cristo? El pan que partimos, ¿no es la comunión del cuerpo de Cristo?» (1 Corintios 10:16, RV1909). Eso es más fuerte que un recordatorio mental. La comunión une a los fieles con Cristo y unos con otros en su cuerpo.

lessonsEs.heading: Real, sacramental, y acercada con temor y fe
lessonsEs.body: La enseñanza ortodoxa no reduce el misterio a un objeto de laboratorio, y no vuelve la Eucaristía un canibalismo burdo. Los dones son verdaderamente el Cuerpo y la Sangre de Cristo por la acción del Espíritu Santo, recibidos sacramentalmente bajo las especies del pan y del vino. San Ignacio de Antioquía ya llamó a la Eucaristía la medicina de la inmortalidad. Porque el don es real, Pablo une la comunión al arrepentimiento, a la reconciliación y al discernimiento.

challenges.title: Essence and energies: truly knowing God
challenges.summary: How St. Gregory Palamas defended real participation in God's life while guarding that the divine essence remains beyond creatures.
challenges.source: Exodus 33 · Matthew 17 · Psalm 36:9 · 2 Peter 1:4 · St. Gregory Palamas

lessons.heading: The Bible holds two truths together
lessons.body: Moses asks to see God's glory and hears that no one can see God's face and live (Exodus 33:20). Paul says God dwells in unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16). Yet the same Bible says God reveals Himself, saves, fills, and gives life. A Christian answer has to protect both: God is not a creature we can comprehend, and God is not absent from the creatures He saves.

lessons.heading: Tabor shows uncreated light, and Peter speaks of participation
lessons.body: At the Transfiguration the disciples see Christ shining with divine glory (Matthew 17:1-8). The Psalm says, in thy light shall we see light (Psalm 36:9). Peter says believers become partakers of the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4). Orthodoxy reads these together: grace is not a created thing placed between us and God. It is God's own life and glory given to creatures, often named His energies.

lessons.heading: Palamas: essence beyond us, energies truly God with us
lessons.body: St. Gregory Palamas defended the hesychast monks by teaching a real distinction: God's essence is what God is in Himself and remains imparticipable to creatures; God's energies are His uncreated activities and life, truly God going forth to create, illumine, and deify. This is not two gods and not a created buffer. We participate in God by grace through His energies, while we never become God by essence.

lessons.heading: The divine names
lessons.body: Dionysius asks the obvious question: how can anyone name the God who is beyond speech and knowledge? Scripture answers by giving names anyway — Wisdom, Truth, Light, Life, Salvation, Righteousness, Love — not because a list of titles equals God, but because people who have met Him must speak. Earthly words and images are the only speech we have. They are true as far as they come from revelation, and they remain too small. Hold both: God is named, and God is never exhausted by the name.

lessons.heading: Cataphatic and apophatic theology
lessons.body: Cataphatic speech says what God has shown: the names and attributes revelation gives. Apophatic speech then refuses to stop there. To call God “being” is already to discover that He is beyond being; every affirmation must be exceeded. The divine darkness is not a mood and not ignorance for its own sake. It is the point past which the intellect cannot carry you. God is met in the depths of prayerful silence — incomprehensible, inaccessible, invisible — and yet truly near. Speculation does not take that last step. Prayer does.

questions.prompt: In the essence-energies distinction, what remains imparticipable to creatures?
choices: God's essence
God's energies
God's glory at Tabor
The life given in grace
questions.explanation: Palamas guards divine transcendence: creatures never comprehend or participate in God's essence as what God is in Himself.

questions.prompt: What do believers participate in by grace?
choices: A created substitute for God
God's uncreated energies and life
The divine essence as a fourth part
Only information about God
questions.explanation: The energies are uncreated: God's own life, glory, and activity. Participation is real, but it is by grace, not by essence.

questions.prompt: Which statement states the distinction without breaking it?
choices: The energies are a second god beside the essence
Grace is only a created gift and not God's own life
God is unknowable in essence and truly known and shared by His energies
To know God means to comprehend the essence
questions.explanation: That sentence keeps both biblical truths: Exodus guards the essence; Tabor and 2 Peter guard real participation.

questions.prompt: Why does Scripture give God many names if no name is enough?
choices: Because each name is a separate god
Because those who have met God must speak, even though earthly words cannot exhaust Him
Because the names were invented to replace prayer
questions.explanation: The names come from encounter and revelation. They let us speak of God without ever summing Him up.

questions.prompt: Which claim matches this reading of the divine names?
choices: A complete list of attributes would be God Himself
God is named truly, and still remains beyond every name
God should never be called Light or Love
questions.explanation: Scripture’s names are real, and none of them, even all together, captures God.

questions.prompt: What is the apophatic move with the names of God?
choices: To deny that God has revealed anything
To say the revealed names, then confess that God transcends every one of them
To treat the sum of the attributes as a definition that captures God
questions.explanation: Apophatic theology does not discard revelation. It confesses that God is beyond every name revelation gives.

questions.prompt: Where does this reading say the soul meets the God who is beyond everything?
choices: In speculative knowledge alone
In prayerful silence
By refusing to pray until every term is defined
questions.explanation: The meeting is in prayerful silence, not in speculation that tries to finish God.

challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessonsEs.heading: La Biblia sostiene juntas dos verdades
lessonsEs.body: Moisés pide ver la gloria de Dios y oye que nadie puede ver el rostro de Dios y vivir: «No podrás ver mi rostro: porque no me verá hombre, y vivirá» (Éxodo 33:20, RV1909). Pablo dice que Dios habita en luz inaccesible: «que habita en luz inaccesible; á quien ninguno de los hombres ha visto ni puede ver» (1 Timoteo 6:16, RV1909). Y la misma Biblia dice que Dios se revela, salva, llena y da vida. Una respuesta cristiana tiene que proteger las dos cosas: Dios no es una criatura que podamos comprender, y Dios no está ausente de las criaturas que salva.

lessonsEs.heading: El Tabor muestra luz increada, y Pedro habla de participación
lessonsEs.body: En la Transfiguración, los discípulos ven a Cristo resplandecer con la gloria divina (Mateo 17:1-8): «resplandeció su rostro como el sol, y sus vestidos fueron blancos como la luz» (Mateo 17:2, RV1909). El salmo dice: «en tu luz veremos la luz» (Salmos 36:9, RV1909). Pedro dice que los creyentes llegan a ser participantes de la naturaleza divina: «para que por ellas fueseis hechos participantes de la naturaleza divina» (2 Pedro 1:4, RV1909). La Ortodoxia lee esto junto: la gracia no es una cosa creada puesta entre nosotros y Dios. Es la propia vida y gloria de Dios dadas a las criaturas, a menudo llamadas sus energías.

La Ortodoxia lee esto junto: la gracia no es una cosa creada puesta entre nosotros y Dios. Es la propia vida y gloria de Dios dadas a las criaturas, a menudo llamadas sus energías.

lessonsEs.heading: Palamás: la esencia más allá de nosotros, las energías verdaderamente Dios con nosotros
lessonsEs.body: San Gregorio Palamás defendió a los monjes hesicastas enseñando una distinción real: la esencia de Dios es lo que Dios es en sí mismo y permanece imparticipable para las criaturas; las energías de Dios son sus actividades y su vida increadas, verdaderamente Dios saliendo para crear, iluminar y deificar. Esto no son dos dioses ni un amortiguador creado. Participamos de Dios por gracia mediante sus energías, y nunca llegamos a ser Dios por esencia.

Esto no son dos dioses ni un amortiguador creado. Participamos de Dios por gracia mediante sus energías, y nunca llegamos a ser Dios por esencia.

lessonsEs.heading: Los nombres divinos
lessonsEs.body: Dionisio hace la pregunta obvia: ¿cómo puede alguien nombrar al Dios que está más allá del habla y del conocimiento? La Escritura responde dando nombres de todos modos: Sabiduría, Verdad, Luz, Vida, Salvación, Justicia, Amor. No porque una lista de títulos equivalga a Dios, sino porque quienes lo han encontrado tienen que hablar. Las palabras y las imágenes de la tierra son el único habla que tenemos. Son verdaderas en cuanto vienen de la revelación, y siguen siendo demasiado pequeñas. Guarda las dos cosas: Dios es nombrado, y Dios nunca se agota en el nombre.

lessonsEs.heading: Teología catafática y apofática
lessonsEs.body: El habla catafática dice lo que Dios ha mostrado: los nombres y los atributos que da la revelación. El habla apofática se niega después a quedarse ahí. Llamar a Dios «ser» es ya descubrir que está más allá del ser; toda afirmación tiene que ser sobrepasada. La tiniebla divina no es un estado de ánimo ni ignorancia por la ignorancia misma. Es el punto más allá del cual el intelecto no puede llevarte. A Dios se lo encuentra en la hondura del silencio orante: incomprensible, inaccesible, invisible, y sin embargo verdaderamente cerca. La especulación no da ese último paso. La oración sí.

challenges.title: Pronounce the Faith I: God and Christ
challenges.summary: Learn to say the big words of the faith out loud — hypostasis, homoousios, Theotokos, communicatio idiomatum — and explain each one in a single clean sentence.
challenges.source: Philippians 2:5-11 · Luke 1:43 · the councils of Nicaea, Ephesus, and Chalcedon

lessons.heading: Three words for who God is
lessons.body: Say them slowly first. Ousia (oo-SEE-ah) means essence or being — what God is. Hypostasis (high-PAH-stuh-sis) means the concrete Person — who God is. Physis (FEE-sis) means nature — what a thing is and how it acts. Explain it clean like this: "God is one ousia in three hypostases. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are not three gods, because they share one divine nature; and they are not one Person wearing masks, because each Person is truly distinct." When a friend says "three Persons means three gods," that sentence is your whole answer.

lessons.heading: One word that guards the Son
lessons.body: Homoousios (hoh-moh-OO-see-ahs) means "of one essence" — the Son is the same in being as the Father, not merely similar to him. Nicaea chose this word in 325 because every softer word left room for the Son to be a creature. Explain it like this: "Jesus is not almost God or partly God. Whatever the Father is as God, the Son is, because they share one essence." The difference between homoousios (same essence) and homoiousios (similar essence) is one small letter — and the whole gospel. The Church fought for the small letter because salvation needs a Savior who is truly God.

lessons.heading: Theotokos, kenosis, communicatio idiomatum
lessons.body: Theotokos (theh-oh-TOH-kohs) means God-bearer: the title for Mary because the child she bore is God the Son in the flesh (Luke 1:43). Kenosis (keh-NOH-sis) means self-emptying, from Philippians 2:7 — the Son emptied himself not by losing divinity but by taking a servant's form. Communicatio idiomatum (kah-myoo-nih-KAH-tee-oh ih-dee-OH-mah-tum) means the exchange of properties: because Christ is one Person in two natures, we can say "God suffered in the flesh" and "the man Jesus is Lord of glory," without mixing the natures. Explain it like this: "Whatever either nature does, the one Person does — so the cross is truly God's own suffering for us, in the flesh."

questions.prompt: What does homoousios confess about the Son?
choices: He is similar in essence to the Father
He is of one essence with the Father — truly God
He is the Father's first creature
questions.explanation: Homoousios means of one essence: the Son is what the Father is as God, not a similar being and not a creature.

questions.prompt: A friend says, "Three Persons means three gods." What is the cleanest first reply?
choices: "The Persons are three separate beings who cooperate"
"One God: Father, Son, and Spirit are distinct Persons sharing one divine nature"
"The word Trinity is not in the Bible, so it does not matter"
questions.explanation: One ousia, three hypostases: distinct Persons, one divine nature — not three gods, and not one Person in disguise.

questions.prompt: Why do we call Mary Theotokos (God-bearer)?
choices: Because she is the source of Christ's divinity
Because the child she bore is God the Son in the flesh — the title guards who Jesus is
Because the Church honors her above God
questions.explanation: Theotokos is a Christological title: it confesses that the one born of Mary is God the Son himself (Luke 1:43; Ephesus, 431).

questions.prompt: What does communicatio idiomatum let us say truthfully?
choices: That the divine nature suffered by itself, apart from the flesh
That the one Person of Christ both was born of Mary and is eternal God, because the properties of both natures belong to the one Person
That the two natures merged into one mixed nature
questions.explanation: The exchange of properties follows from one Person in two unconfused natures: born of Mary according to the flesh, eternal according to divinity.

lessonsEs.heading: Tres palabras para quién es Dios
lessonsEs.body: Dí las tres despacio primero. Ousía (u-sí-a) significa esencia o ser: lo que Dios es. Hipóstasis (i-pós-ta-sis) significa la Persona concreta: quién es Dios. Fisis (fí-sis) significa naturaleza: lo que algo es y cómo actúa. Explícalo con limpieza así: «Dios es una sola ousía en tres hipóstasis. El Padre, el Hijo y el Espíritu Santo no son tres dioses, porque comparten una sola naturaleza divina; y no son una Persona con máscaras, porque cada Persona es verdaderamente distinta». Cuando un amigo dice «tres Personas significan tres dioses», esa frase es toda tu respuesta.

lessonsEs.heading: Una palabra que guarda al Hijo
lessonsEs.body: Homoousios (jo-mo-ú-si-os) significa «de una sola esencia»: el Hijo es lo mismo en el ser que el Padre, no meramente parecido a él. Nicea eligió esta palabra en el año 325 porque cada palabra más blanda dejaba espacio para que el Hijo fuera criatura. Explícalo así: «Jesús no es casi Dios ni Dios a medias. Lo que el Padre es como Dios, el Hijo lo es, porque comparten una sola esencia». La diferencia entre homoousios (la misma esencia) y homoiousios (esencia semejante) es una letra pequeña, y el evangelio entero. La Iglesia peleó por esa letra pequeña porque la salvación necesita un Salvador que sea verdaderamente Dios.

lessonsEs.heading: Theotokos, kénosis, communicatio idiomatum
lessonsEs.body: Theotokos (te-o-tó-kos) significa la que dio a luz a Dios: el título de María porque el niño que dio a luz es Dios el Hijo en la carne (Lucas 1:43: «la madre de mi Señor», RV1909). Kénosis (ké-no-sis) significa despojarse de sí, a partir de Filipenses 2:7: el Hijo se anonadó no perdiendo la divinidad, sino tomando forma de siervo. «Sin embargo, se anonadó á sí mismo, tomando forma de siervo, hecho semejante á los hombres» (Filipenses 2:7, RV1909). Communicatio idiomatum (co-mu-ni-ca-cio i-dio-má-tum) significa la comunicación de propiedades: porque Cristo es una Persona en dos naturalezas, podemos decir «Dios padeció en la carne» y «el hombre Jesús es Señor de gloria», sin mezclar las naturalezas. Explícalo así: «Lo que hace cualquiera de las dos naturalezas, lo hace la única Persona; así la cruz es de verdad el propio padecimiento de Dios por nosotros, en la carne».

challenges.title: Pronounce the Faith II: Grace and the inner life
challenges.summary: Perichoresis, theosis, synergeia, logismoi, krasis, the gnomic will — say the words of the Christian life out loud and learn to explain each one plainly.
challenges.source: 2 Peter 1:4 · John 17:21-23 · St. Maximus the Confessor · St. John of Damascus

lessons.heading: Perichoresis and theosis
lessons.body: Perichoresis (peh-ree-koh-REE-sis) means mutual indwelling: the Father, Son, and Spirit dwell in one another without confusion, and Christ prays that we would be drawn into that same communion (John 17:21). Theosis (theh-OH-sis) means deification: by grace we become "partakers of the divine nature" (2 Peter 1:4) — not God by essence, but truly united to God by his uncreated energies. Explain it like this: "God does not only forgive us from far away. He gives us his own life, the way fire makes iron glow: the iron stays iron, but it burns with the fire's heat."

lessons.heading: Synergeia: God does not save us without us
lessons.body: Synergeia (sin-EHR-gee-ah) means synergy, working-together. Salvation is neither God dragging a puppet nor man climbing alone. The classic line runs: "He who created you without you will not save you without you" (St. Augustine). Grace heals and elevates the will; it never coerces it. Explain it with your hands: "God opens the door and gives me the strength to walk — but the walking is really mine. He treats me as a person, not a stone." A stone is moved wholly from outside; a son is moved by love from inside, and his yes is genuinely his own.

lessons.heading: Logismoi, krasis, and the gnomic will
lessons.body: Logismoi (loh-geez-MEE) are the assaultive thoughts or urges — Evagrius listed eight that take turns pressing on the soul: gluttony, lust, greed, sadness, anger, acedia (listless despair), vainglory, pride. Krasis (KRAH-sis) is the mixture or temperament of body and soul; Nemesius of Emesa taught that different mixtures incline different people toward different ruling passions. Thelema gnomikon (THEH-leh-mah noh-MEE-kon) is the gnomic will, St. Maximus's term for our personal, deliberating way of choosing, shaped by temperament and history. Explain it like this: "The fall is one wound, but it bleeds differently in each person. The Fathers diagnose your ruling passion before they prescribe your cure."

questions.prompt: What does theosis mean?
choices: Becoming God by essence, equal to the Father
Partaking of the divine nature by grace — united to God without ceasing to be human
Escaping the body to become pure spirit
questions.explanation: Theosis is participation by grace (2 Peter 1:4): real union with God, while the Creator-creature distinction stands forever.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best explains synergeia (synergy)?
choices: God saves us entirely without our involvement, like moving a stone
We save ourselves; God only watches
Grace heals and strengthens the will, and our free yes is genuinely ours — God does not save us without us
questions.explanation: Synergy: grace never coerces, and man never climbs alone. God gives the healing and the strength; the person truly walks.

questions.prompt: What are the logismoi?
choices: The eight deadly sins everyone commits equally
Assaultive urges (gluttony, lust, greed, sadness, anger, acedia, vainglory, pride) that press differently on different souls
The eight beatitudes read backwards
questions.explanation: Evagrius's eight logismoi are urges that take turns ruling different souls — which is why the Philokalia diagnoses the ruling passion first.

questions.prompt: What does krasis (temperament) explain, in Nemesius's teaching?
choices: Why the fall expresses itself through different dominant passions in different people
Why some nations are saved and others are not
Why the body is evil and must be escaped
questions.explanation: Krasis is the body-soul mixture: one fallen condition, many dispositions — so the same wound bleeds differently in each person.

lessonsEs.heading: Perijóresis y teosis
lessonsEs.body: Perijóresis (pe-ri-jó-re-sis) significa inhabitación mutua: el Padre, el Hijo y el Espíritu habitan el uno en el otro sin confusión, y Cristo ora para que seamos atraídos a esa misma comunión (Juan 17:21): «Para que todos sean una cosa; como tú, oh Padre, en mí, y yo en ti, que también ellos sean en nosotros una cosa» (RV1909). Teosis (te-ó-sis) significa deificación: por gracia llegamos a ser «participantes de la naturaleza divina» (2 Pedro 1:4, RV1909). No Dios por esencia, sino unidos de verdad a Dios por sus energías increadas. Explícalo así: «Dios no solo nos perdona desde lejos. Nos da su propia vida, como el fuego hace brillar el hierro: el hierro sigue siendo hierro, pero arde con el calor del fuego».
