challenges.title: Ladder 5 · The Key Figures
challenges.summary: Ladder session 5 of 6. Cyril and Nestorius at Ephesus, Eutyches the counterweight, Maximus who paid with his tongue and hand, and John of Damascus who wrote the summary the Church still uses.
challenges.source: St. Cyril's Letters to Nestorius · St. Maximus, Disputation with Pyrrhus · St. John of Damascus, On the Orthodox Faith III

lessons.heading: Cyril against Nestorius: the fight over one word for Mary
lessons.body: Nestorius (nes-TOR-ee-us), patriarch of Constantinople, balked at calling Mary Theotokos: God cannot be born, he reasoned, so Mary bore the man in whom the Word dwelt. St. Cyril of Alexandria (SEER-il) saw the split instantly. If the one born of Mary is not God the Word himself, then Jesus is two subjects — a man inspired, indwelt, honored — and the cross becomes the death of a man near God, not God's own death for us in the flesh. Cyril pressed the communicatio idiomatum relentlessly: because the Person is one, Scripture's bold sentences stand — God born, God crucified in the flesh. His Twelve Anathemas and the Second and Third Letters to Nestorius became Ephesus's yardstick: whoever will not confess the one incarnate Word, and Mary as Theotokos, has already divided Christ.

lessons.heading: Eutyches and Maximus: the opposite ditch, and the confessor
lessons.body: Eutyches (YOO-tih-keez), an elderly Constantinople archimandrite, hated Nestorius so much he fell off the other side: before the union, two natures; after the union, one — with the humanity so swallowed by divinity that Christ was not consubstantial with us. Chalcedon deposed him and confessed the natures unconfused. Two centuries later St. Maximus the Confessor (MAK-sih-mus) fought the subtler sequel, monothelitism. His tools were the ones from session 1: the human nature is enhypostatic in the Word, real in every faculty — mind, will, energy — and precisely therefore healed. When emperor and patriarchs demanded silence, Maximus would not trade Christ's human will for peace; they cut out his tongue and cut off his right hand, and he died in exile in 662. Constantinople III vindicated him nineteen years after his death.

lessons.heading: John of Damascus: the summary that closed the age
lessons.body: St. John of Damascus (duh-MAS-kus), writing in the 8th century from the monastery of St. Sabbas, gathered the whole patristic settlement into On the Orthodox Faith — the first great summary, and still the Church's handbook. Book III gives Christology its classic form: one hypostasis, two natures, two wills and energies, the communicatio idiomatum with its concrete and abstract rules, and the phrase that threads everything: the Word "became flesh" without ceasing to be what he was, and the flesh became the Word's own without ceasing to be ours. When you meet a new Christological claim, the Damascene is the test bench: does it keep Cyril's one Person, Chalcedon's unconfused natures, and Maximus's complete humanity — mind, will, and all? If it fails any one, it is one of the seven ditches with new paint.

questions.prompt: What did Cyril see at stake in the word Theotokos?
choices: Mary's personal honor in the empire
Whether the one born of Mary is God the Word himself, or a man merely indwelt by God
Whether bishops may preach about Mary
The date of the Annunciation feast
questions.explanation: Split the child, and the cross is a man's death near God — not God's own saving death in the flesh. Ephesus agreed with Cyril.

questions.prompt: Nestorius preferred to protect God by...
choices: Denying Christ's humanity
Joining the Word and the man by will and honor rather than by personal union
Making the Spirit a creature
Blaming the council system
questions.explanation: Indwelling instead of incarnation: two subjects in close alliance. That is precisely what hypostatic union denies.

questions.prompt: Eutyches's error, in one line:
choices: Two persons in Christ
After the union, one nature, with the humanity absorbed so Christ is not consubstantial with us
No human mind in Christ
Sonship by adoption
questions.explanation: The anti-Nestorian overcorrection. Chalcedon: the natures remain, unconfused and unchanged, in one Person.

questions.prompt: What did Maximus the Confessor lose for confessing Christ's human will?
choices: His monastery only
His tongue and his right hand, dying in exile — vindicated at Constantinople III
A debate in Alexandria
His books were edited, nothing more
questions.explanation: Mutilated in 662 for refusing to silence the two wills; the council of 681 confessed exactly what he died for.

questions.prompt: Maximus's word for how Christ's human nature personally exists is...
choices: Anhypostasia alone, floating free
Enhypostasia: it exists in the hypostasis of the Word
A second hypostasis beside the Word
A prosopon added at the resurrection
questions.explanation: Not its own person, and not ungrounded: enhypostatic in the Word, complete in mind, will, and energy — and so healed.

questions.prompt: Why does the Church still test claims by John of Damascus's On the Orthodox Faith?
choices: It is the newest book on the subject
It is the classic summary: Cyril's one Person, Chalcedon's unconfused natures, Maximus's complete humanity in one bench-test
It replaced the councils
It explains Christ in Latin categories
questions.explanation: Written after the councils, gathering them. A claim that fails any of the three has fallen into one of the seven ditches.

lessonsEs.heading: Cirilo contra Nestorio: la pelea por una palabra acerca de María
lessonsEs.body: Nestorio, patriarca de Constantinopla, se resistió a llamar a María Theotokos: Dios no puede nacer, razonaba, así que María dio a luz al hombre en quien habitaba el Verbo. San Cirilo de Alejandría vio la ruptura al instante. Si el nacido de María no es Dios el Verbo mismo, entonces Jesús es dos sujetos: un hombre inspirado, habitado, honrado. Y la cruz se vuelve la muerte de un hombre cerca de Dios, no la propia muerte de Dios por nosotros en la carne. Cirilo apretó sin descanso la communicatio idiomatum: porque la Persona es una, se sostienen las frases audaces de la Escritura: Dios nacido, Dios crucificado en la carne. Sus Doce Anatemas y la Segunda y la Tercera Carta a Nestorio se volvieron la vara de medir de Éfeso: quien no confiese al único Verbo encarnado, y a María como Theotokos, ya ha dividido a Cristo.

lessonsEs.heading: Eutiques y Máximo: la zanja de enfrente, y el confesor
lessonsEs.body: Eutiques, un archimandrita anciano de Constantinopla, odiaba tanto a Nestorio que se cayó del otro lado: antes de la unión, dos naturalezas; después de la unión, una, con la humanidad tan tragada por la divinidad que Cristo no era consustancial con nosotros. Calcedonia lo depuso y confesó las naturalezas sin confusión. Dos siglos después, san Máximo el Confesor peleó la secuela más sutil, el monotelismo. Sus herramientas eran las de la primera lección de esta escalera: la naturaleza humana es enhipostática en el Verbo, real en cada facultad —mente, voluntad, energía— y precisamente por eso sanada. Cuando el emperador y los patriarcas exigieron silencio, Máximo no cambió la voluntad humana de Cristo por la paz; le cortaron la lengua y le cortaron la mano derecha, y murió en el exilio en el año 662. Constantinopla III lo vindicó diecinueve años después de su muerte.

lessonsEs.bodyEs: Eutiques, un archimandrita anciano de Constantinopla, odiaba tanto a Nestorio que se cayó del otro lado: antes de la unión, dos naturalezas; después de la unión, una, con la humanidad tan tragada por la divinidad que Cristo no era consustancial con nosotros. Calcedonia lo depuso y confesó las naturalezas sin confusión. Dos siglos después, san Máximo el Confesor peleó la secuela más sutil, el monotelismo. Sus herramientas eran las de la primera lección de esta escalera: la naturaleza humana es enhipostática en el Verbo, real en cada facultad —mente, voluntad, energía— y precisamente por eso sanada. Cuando el emperador y los patriarcas exigieron silencio, Máximo no cambió la voluntad humana de Cristo por la paz; le cortaron la lengua y le cortaron la mano derecha, y murió en el exilio en el año 662. Constantinopla III lo vindicó diecinueve años después de su muerte.

lessonsEs.heading: Juan Damasceno: el resumen que cerró la época
lessonsEs.body: San Juan Damasceno, escribiendo en el siglo octavo desde el monasterio de san Sabas, reunió todo el asentamiento patrístico en Sobre la fe ortodoxa: el primer gran resumen, y todavía el manual de la Iglesia. El libro tercero le da a la cristología su forma clásica: una hipóstasis, dos naturalezas, dos voluntades y energías, la communicatio idiomatum con sus reglas concreta y abstracta, y la frase que lo enhebra todo: el Verbo «se hizo carne» sin dejar de ser lo que era, y la carne se volvió propia del Verbo sin dejar de ser nuestra. Cuando te encuentres una afirmación cristológica nueva, el Damasceno es el banco de prueba: ¿guarda la única Persona de Cirilo, las naturalezas sin confusión de Calcedonia y la humanidad completa de Máximo, mente, voluntad y todo? Si falla en cualquiera, es una de las siete zanjas con pintura nueva.

challenges.title: Ladder 6 · The Orthodox Terms
challenges.summary: Ladder session 6 of 6. The wider Orthodox vocabulary the Christology stands in: Panagia, ousia and energies, the essence-energies distinction, theosis, perichoresis, and prosopon.
challenges.source: 2 Peter 1:4 · John 17:21-23 · St. Gregory Palamas, the Triads

lessons.heading: Panagia, and the map of essence and energies
lessons.body: Panagia (pah-nah-GEE-ah) means All-Holy, the Church's beloved title for Mary — the one whose holiness is wholly gift, as ours is meant to be. Around her, the Damascene and St. Gregory Palamas draw the map this whole ladder stands in. Ousia (oo-SEE-ah), essence, answers what God is: the divine being itself, utterly beyond creaturely comprehension — no one has known, or can know, what God is in himself (Exodus 33:20; 1 Timothy 6:16). The energies (EN-er-jeez) answer what God does: his uncreated operations and gifts — life, light, grace, the glory of Tabor — truly God, truly given. The essence-energies distinction holds both: God is unknowable in essence and genuinely knowable in his energies, as the sun is untouchable in its core and warm on your skin.

lessons.heading: Theosis and perichoresis: where the map leads
lessons.body: Theosis (theh-OH-sis) is the destination: becoming by grace what God is by nature — "partakers of the divine nature" (2 Peter 1:4). Not absorption (the Eutychian ditch in mystical dress) and not moral improvement alone: real participation in the uncreated life, while we remain creatures forever. Perichoresis (peh-ree-koh-REE-sis) names the shape of that life in God himself: the mutual indwelling of the Persons — the Father in the Son, the Son in the Father, the Spirit in both — distinct without distance, one without confusion. The same word serves Christology (the natures interpenetrate in the one Person without mixing) and the Trinity, and it is why salvation is pictured as being drawn into a communion that already exists, not admitted to a crowd: "that they all may be one, as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee" (John 17:21).

lessons.heading: Prosopon: the face of the Person
lessons.body: Prosopon (PROH-soh-pon) is the Greek word for face, and in theology for the person as presented — the one you meet, address, and love. It carries both riches and a warning from the ladder's first rungs: in sloppy hands prosopon shrank toward mask or role (the old Sabellian danger, as if the Persons were faces God wears). The councils therefore anchored it: prosopon is true speech when it means hypostasis — a real, distinct who, not a costume. Say the whole ladder back now: one God, one ousia, three hypostases (never three prosopa as masks); in Christ, one hypostasis and prosopon of the Word, two natures with all their idioms, two wills, and the energies of God given to us for theosis. That is the faith of the sessions — hold it, and you can hear any new claim and know within a sentence which ditch it leans toward.

questions.explanation: Untouchable core, real warmth: we participate in God himself by his energies, while his essence remains forever beyond creatures.

questions.prompt: Perichoresis names...

questions.prompt: Why did the councils treat prosopon carefully?
choices: It is a Latin word they distrusted

questions.explanation: Face and person — true when anchored to hypostasis, dangerous when it slides toward three masks of one actor.

questions.prompt: Which sentence recites the whole ladder cleanly?
choices: One God in three masks; Christ a God-filled man; salvation by example

questions.explanation: That is the six sessions in one breath — Godhead, union, properties, heresies avoided, councils, figures, and terms all held together.

lessonsEs.heading: Panagia, y el mapa de la esencia y las energías
lessonsEs.body: Panagia (pa-na-gí-a) significa Toda-Santa, el título querido de la Iglesia para María: aquella cuya santidad es enteramente don, como la nuestra está llamada a ser. Alrededor de ella, el Damasceno y san Gregorio Palamás trazan el mapa en el que se sostiene toda esta escalera. Ousía (u-sí-a), esencia, responde qué es Dios: el ser divino mismo, del todo más allá de la comprensión de la criatura. Nadie ha conocido, ni puede conocer, qué es Dios en sí mismo (Éxodo 33:20; 1 Timoteo 6:16). Las energías responden qué hace Dios: sus operaciones y dones increados —vida, luz, gracia, la gloria del Tabor—, verdaderamente Dios, verdaderamente dados. La distinción entre esencia y energías sostiene las dos: Dios es incognoscible en su esencia y genuinamente cognoscible en sus energías, como el sol es intocable en su núcleo y cálido en tu piel.

lessonsEs.heading: Teosis y perijóresis: adonde lleva el mapa
lessonsEs.body: La teosis (te-ó-sis) es el destino: llegar por gracia a ser lo que Dios es por naturaleza, «participantes de la naturaleza divina» (2 Pedro 1:4, RV1909). No absorción (la zanja eutiquiana con vestido místico) y no solo mejora moral: participación real en la vida increada, mientras permanecemos criaturas para siempre. Perijóresis (pe-ri-jó-re-sis) nombra la forma de esa vida en Dios mismo: la inhabitación mutua de las Personas. El Padre en el Hijo, el Hijo en el Padre, el Espíritu en ambos, distintos sin distancia, uno sin confusión. La misma palabra sirve a la cristología (las naturalezas se interpenetran en la única Persona sin mezclarse) y a la Trinidad, y por eso la salvación se dibuja como ser atraído a una comunión que ya existe, no como ser admitido a una multitud: «Para que todos sean una cosa; como tú, oh Padre, en mí, y yo en ti» (Juan 17:21, RV1909).

lessonsEs.heading: Prosopon: el rostro de la Persona
lessonsEs.body: Prosopon (pró-so-pon) es la palabra griega para rostro, y en teología para la persona tal como se presenta: aquel a quien encuentras, a quien te diriges y a quien amas. Carga riquezas y una advertencia desde los primeros peldaños de la escalera: en manos descuidadas, prosopon se encogió hacia máscara o papel (el viejo peligro sabeliano, como si las Personas fueran rostros que Dios se pone). Los concilios por eso lo anclaron: prosopon es habla verdadera cuando significa hipóstasis, un quién real y distinto, no un disfraz. Di ahora toda la escalera de nuevo: un solo Dios, una ousía, tres hipóstasis (nunca tres prosopa como máscaras); en Cristo, una hipóstasis y un prosopon del Verbo, dos naturalezas con todos sus idiomas, dos voluntades, y las energías de Dios dadas a nosotros para la teosis. Esa es la fe de estas lecciones. Guárdala, y podrás oír cualquier afirmación nueva y saber, en una frase, hacia qué zanja se inclina.

challenges.title: Dogma and spirituality
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Dogma is not an optional preface to Christian life. Faith and a moral life belong together, and so do doctrine and prayer.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Dogma and spirituality
lessons.body: A common modern habit treats dogma as optional history and keeps morality or social programs as the real Christian work. That split contradicts the faith itself. James says faith without works is dead. Paul says a person is justified by faith apart from works of the law — meaning the old rites and sacrifices, not mercy and obedience. Good deeds do not purchase salvation, and faith does not float free of a moral life. The same is true of doctrine and prayer. Dogma and mysticism lead to the one Truth, who is Christ. Orthodox theology, from Paul and Ignatius to Theophan and Silouan, starts in spiritual experience rather than in a system that never prays. Christianity does not answer every curiosity. It opens a reality before which the soul grows quiet.

questions.prompt: What does this reading refuse to separate?
choices: Dogma from moral life, and doctrine from prayer
Christ from the Gospels
The Father from any mention of love
questions.explanation: Dogma and life belong together. Faith without works is dead, and works without faith do not save. Doctrine and spirituality are the same life.

questions.prompt: What did Paul mean by “works of the law” in this reading?
choices: The Old Testament rites and sacrifices, which Christ’s offering fulfills
Every good deed, which Paul forbids
Prayer, which he treats as optional
questions.explanation: “Works of the law” names the rites that followed the old covenant, not mercy. Justification by faith still walks with a moral life.

questions.prompt: Where does Orthodox theology start, in this reading?
choices: In spiritual experience, from the apostles to the recent saints
In a system that never needs to pray
In answering every question the mind can invent
questions.explanation: The Fathers’ theology proceeds from life with God. Christianity opens a mystery; it does not close every curiosity.

lessonsEs.heading: El dogma y la espiritualidad
lessonsEs.body: Una costumbre moderna común trata el dogma como historia opcional y guarda la moral o los programas sociales como el verdadero trabajo cristiano. Esa ruptura contradice la fe misma. Santiago dice que la fe sin obras está muerta. Pablo dice que la persona es justificada por la fe aparte de las obras de la ley: quiere decir los ritos y sacrificios antiguos, no la misericordia y la obediencia. Las buenas obras no compran la salvación, y la fe no flota libre de una vida moral. Lo mismo vale para la doctrina y la oración. El dogma y la mística conducen a la única Verdad, que es Cristo. La teología ortodoxa, desde Pablo e Ignacio hasta Teófano y Siluán, empieza en la experiencia espiritual y no en un sistema que nunca ora. El cristianismo no responde cada curiosidad. Abre una realidad ante la cual el alma se queda quieta.

La teología ortodoxa, desde Pablo e Ignacio hasta Teófano y Siluán, empieza en la experiencia espiritual y no en un sistema que nunca ora. El cristianismo no responde cada curiosidad. Abre una realidad ante la cual el alma se queda quieta.

challenges.title: Faith, the call, and conversion
challenges.level: 3 teaching cards · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Faith is an encounter God begins. The call can be heard in a noisy life, and conversion has as many paths as there are persons.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: What is faith?
lessons.body: Faith is the path on which we meet God, and God takes the first step. He believes in us before we believe in Him, and gives some sign of His presence. Our first move is an answer. The Galilean fishermen drop their nets at “Follow me.” The rich young man hears the same call and goes away sad, because he has treasure on earth. Poverty of spirit is the blessing: to know that nothing you own can stand in for God, and to hunger for Him with soul, mind, and will.

lessons.heading: The call
lessons.body: The call is easy to miss. A life filled with work can leave no silence in which God is heard, and religion can shrink to a holiday kept for the sake of roots. Even so, the call still comes — sometimes only as restlessness. Augustine’s line belongs here: we were made for God, and our hearts are restless until they rest in Him. The costly mistake is to recognize the voice years after it spoke. Answer when He speaks. That answer can transfigure a whole life.

lessons.heading: Conversion to God
lessons.body: No two people come to God by the same road. The meeting may be sudden or slow, in childhood or in old age. Often the seeker thinks he has found God, and later sees that God found him. Augustine’s long reading, a collapse of health or hope, the face of a believer, or a religious family — all of these are real paths, and none of them is automatic. Faith received from one’s parents still has to become one’s own. Faith is a gift. It is often given through the effort of the person who asked for it.

questions.prompt: Who takes the first step in faith?
choices: God, who gives a sign of His presence
The believer, who must become worthy first
No one; faith is a guess
questions.explanation: Faith is an encounter God opens. Our first step is a response.

questions.prompt: How may God’s call arrive in a noisy life?
choices: As restlessness or inner unease, not only as a voice we already understand
Only through a holiday custom
It cannot be heard at all in the modern world
questions.explanation: The call can feel like dissatisfaction or a search, and only later be recognized as God. Augustine: the heart is restless until it rests in Him.

questions.prompt: What is true of conversion?
choices: There is one approved path, and every believer must copy it
Every path is personal, and even a family faith must become one’s own
God never seeks; only the energetic find Him
questions.explanation: No two roads are the same. Faith is a gift, often given through the seeker’s own effort, and inherited faith still has to be personally lived.

challenges.titleEs: La fe, el llamado y la conversión
challenges.summaryEs: La fe es confiar y volverse, no firmar una lista de ideas.

lessonsEs.heading: ¿Qué es la fe?
lessonsEs.body: La fe es el camino en el que encontramos a Dios, y Dios da el primer paso. Él cree en nosotros antes de que nosotros creamos en él, y da alguna señal de su presencia. Nuestro primer movimiento es una respuesta. Los pescadores de Galilea sueltan las redes ante «Sígueme». El joven rico oye el mismo llamado y se va triste, porque tiene tesoro en la tierra. La pobreza de espíritu es la bienaventuranza: saber que nada de lo que posees puede ocupar el lugar de Dios, y tener hambre de él con el alma, la mente y la voluntad.

La pobreza de espíritu es la bienaventuranza: saber que nada de lo que posees puede ocupar el lugar de Dios, y tener hambre de él con el alma, la mente y la voluntad.

lessonsEs.heading: El llamado
lessonsEs.body: El llamado es fácil de perder. Una vida llena de trabajo puede no dejar silencio en el que se oiga a Dios, y la religión puede encogerse a un día de fiesta guardado por las raíces. Aun así, el llamado sigue llegando, a veces solo como inquietud. Aquí cabe la frase de Agustín: fuimos hechos para Dios, y nuestro corazón está inquieto hasta que descansa en él. El error costoso es reconocer la voz años después de que habló. Responde cuando él habla. Esa respuesta puede transfigurar una vida entera.

lessonsEs.heading: La conversión a Dios
lessonsEs.body: No hay dos personas que lleguen a Dios por el mismo camino. El encuentro puede ser súbito o lento, en la niñez o en la vejez. A menudo el que busca cree que encontró a Dios, y después ve que Dios lo encontró a él. La larga lectura de Agustín, un derrumbe de la salud o de la esperanza, el rostro de un creyente o una familia religiosa: todos estos son caminos reales, y ninguno es automático. La fe recibida de los padres todavía tiene que volverse propia. La fe es un don. A menudo se da por medio del esfuerzo de la persona que la pidió.

challenges.title: From philosophy to revelation
challenges.level: 2 teaching cards · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Greek thought came near the truth and then stopped. Israel knew God because God spoke and walked with a people.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Philosophy in search of a supreme Good
lessons.body: From the beginning, people have hunted for the meaning of being. Greek philosophy studied the world, the mind, and the first causes, and often joined that study to ascetic discipline, a purification of mind and body. The order of things — the cosmos, as against chaos — suggested a Maker. Plato could speak of Creator, Father, and Craftsman, and of the Logos. Plotinus pressed further: the One beyond every definition, then Intelligence and Soul, a triad, with the world as a reflection of the divine. Early Christian writers could call such philosophers Christians before Christ. Near is not the same as arrival. Philosophy can see the foothills. It cannot climb the mountain by itself.

lessons.heading: The Old Testament: divine revelation
lessons.body: Most of the ancient world worshipped many gods. Israel was entrusted with something else: knowledge of God, of creation, and of why we exist, learned not only from books but from a long experience. Noah, Abraham, Moses, Elijah, and the righteous of Israel spoke with God and walked before Him. This God is not an abstract force. He speaks, hears, and acts. He goes before the people as fire, and He consents to dwell in the house they build, though heaven and earth cannot contain Him. The God of the philosophers stays distant and lifeless by comparison. Both paths confess that God is a mystery. Philosophy stops at the foothills. Revelation takes people up the mountain.

questions.prompt: Why did some early Christians call Greek philosophers “Christians before Christ”?
choices: Because Plato and Plotinus had already come near the one God, the Logos, and a divine triad
Because Greek religion was already the Church
Because philosophy replaces the Bible
questions.explanation: They came near: one Maker, the Logos, a triad, the vision of God. Near is not yet revelation.

questions.prompt: How did Israel know God, in this reading?
choices: By age-long encounter: God spoke, led, and dwelt among them
Only by copying Greek metaphysics
By concluding that God is an impersonal law
questions.explanation: Revelation is personal. The God of Israel is living and near, and still mysterious.

questions.prompt: Where does philosophy stop, and revelation go on?
choices: Philosophy remains at the foothills; revelation leads up the mountain
They teach exactly the same thing
Revelation forbids anyone to think
questions.explanation: Both confess the mystery. Only revelation brings a person into the presence of the living God.

challenges.titleEs: De la filosofía a la revelación
challenges.summaryEs: Pensar ayuda. Dios también habla, y no solo desde nuestros argumentos.

lessonsEs.heading: La filosofía en busca de un Bien supremo
lessonsEs.body: Desde el principio, la gente ha buscado el sentido del ser. La filosofía griega estudió el mundo, la mente y las causas primeras, y a menudo unió ese estudio a la disciplina ascética, una purificación de la mente y del cuerpo. El orden de las cosas —el cosmos, frente al caos— sugería un Hacedor. Platón podía hablar de Creador, Padre y Artífice, y del Logos. Plotino fue más lejos: el Uno más allá de toda definición, después la Inteligencia y el Alma, una tríada, con el mundo como reflejo de lo divino. Los escritores cristianos antiguos podían llamar a tales filósofos cristianos antes de Cristo. Estar cerca no es lo mismo que llegar. La filosofía puede ver las faldas del monte. No puede escalar la montaña por sí sola.

No puede escalar la montaña por sí sola.

lessonsEs.heading: El Antiguo Testamento: revelación divina
lessonsEs.body: La mayor parte del mundo antiguo adoraba a muchos dioses. A Israel se le confió otra cosa: el conocimiento de Dios, de la creación y de por qué existimos, aprendido no solo de libros sino de una larga experiencia. Noé, Abraham, Moisés, Elías y los justos de Israel hablaron con Dios y caminaron delante de él. Este Dios no es una fuerza abstracta. Habla, oye y actúa. Va delante del pueblo como fuego, y consiente en habitar la casa que le construyen, aunque el cielo y la tierra no pueden contenerlo. El Dios de los filósofos se queda distante y sin vida en comparación. Los dos caminos confiesan que Dios es un misterio. La filosofía se detiene en las faldas del monte. La revelación lleva a las personas montaña arriba.

challenges.title: The angels
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: “Heavens and earth” names two creations: the invisible spiritual world and the visible world. The angels worship, serve, and remain distinct from humanity.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: The angels
lessons.body: “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth” has long been heard as two worlds: one invisible, spiritual, and intelligible, and one visible and material. The angels belong to the first. Isaiah sees seraphim around the Lord crying “Holy, holy, holy.” They are not a decoration of the vision. They are creatures who worship. Gregory of Nyssa reads the parable of the lost sheep with the same map: the ninety-nine who never left the hills are the angels, and the one sheep the shepherd seeks is the human race. Human beings are not angels, and angels are not a substitute for the Incarnation. God assumed human nature, not an angelic one. Honor the angels as fellow servants who praise God and care for the race He came to save.

questions.prompt: What do “the heavens and the earth” name in this reading?
choices: The invisible spiritual creation and the visible material creation
Two equal gods
Only the sky and the soil, with no spiritual world

As the demons
questions.explanation: The ninety-nine who stayed in the hills are the angels. The lost sheep is humanity.

questions.prompt: Which nature did God assume in the Incarnation?
choices: Human nature, not angelic nature
Angelic nature, instead of ours
Neither; God only appeared
questions.explanation: The angels remain creatures who worship and serve. The Son took our nature, not theirs.

lessonsEs.heading: Los ángeles
lessonsEs.body: «En el principio crió Dios los cielos y la tierra» (Génesis 1:1, RV1909) se ha oído desde hace mucho como dos mundos: uno invisible, espiritual e inteligible, y otro visible y material. Los ángeles pertenecen al primero. Isaías ve serafines alrededor del Señor clamando «Santo, santo, santo» (Isaías 6:3). No son un adorno de la visión. Son criaturas que adoran. Gregorio de Nisa lee la parábola de la oveja perdida con el mismo mapa: las noventa y nueve que nunca dejaron los montes son los ángeles, y la oveja que el pastor busca es la raza humana. Los seres humanos no son ángeles, y los ángeles no sustituyen la Encarnación. Dios asumió la naturaleza humana, no una angélica. Honra a los ángeles como consiervos que alaban a Dios y cuidan de la raza que él vino a salvar.

challenges.title: The origin of evil
challenges.level: 2 teaching cards · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Evil is not a second god and not a substance. It begins in a created will that turns away, and it becomes active in the devil and the demons.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: The origin of evil
lessons.body: Before the visible world, and after the angels were made, a catastrophe struck, known now by its wreckage. Angels were meant to grow in virtue until they were as like God as a creature can be. Some refused. From then on the world is a field of two unequal powers: God, and the devil who is not His rival equal. Dualism is the mistake to refuse — the idea that light and darkness, spirit and matter, are two eternal kingdoms. Matter is not evil. Evil is not a substance that has always existed. Basil says it plainly: evil is not a living substance but a condition of the soul, as shadow is the absence of light. Lucifer was created good. He ruined his own goodness by the freedom he was given, and fell from the Source of good.

lessons.heading: The evil-doer
lessons.body: Evil has no being of its own. It becomes an agent of ruin when it is taken up into a person: the devil and the demons. That is what it means to say evil was “hypostasized.” It is still a parasite on good. Scripture can speak of God “creating evil” or sending a lying spirit, and those lines have to be read without making God the author of wickedness. He remains Lord over good and evil in the sense that He can allow an evil will and bend its consequences toward good. His thoughts are not our thoughts. The devil is real, defeated in advance, and not a second creator.

questions.prompt: What is evil, according to St Basil in this reading?
choices: Not a living substance, but a condition of the soul — the absence of good
A god equal to the God of light, ruling matter forever
The material world itself
questions.explanation: Evil is a falling away from good, not a coeternal substance. Matter is not the evil kingdom.

questions.prompt: How did the devil become the devil?
choices: A good angel abused his freedom and fell from the Source of goodness

challenges.summaryEs: El mal no es un segundo dios. Es un bien torcido, y la Escritura lo cuenta así.

lessonsEs.heading: El origen del mal
lessonsEs.body: Antes del mundo visible, y después de que los ángeles fueron hechos, golpeó una catástrofe, conocida ahora por sus escombros. Los ángeles estaban llamados a crecer en la virtud hasta ser tan semejantes a Dios como una criatura puede serlo. Algunos se negaron. Desde entonces el mundo es un campo de dos poderes desiguales: Dios, y el diablo, que no es su rival igual. El dualismo es el error que hay que rechazar: la idea de que la luz y la tiniebla, el espíritu y la materia, son dos reinos eternos. La materia no es mala. El mal no es una sustancia que siempre haya existido. Basilio lo dice con claridad: el mal no es una sustancia viva, sino una condición del alma, como la sombra es la ausencia de luz. Lucifer fue creado bueno. Arruinó su propia bondad con la libertad que se le dio, y cayó de la Fuente del bien.

challenges.title: The human person
challenges.level: 3 teaching cards · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Humanity is the crown of creation: one nature of soul and body, free, made in the image of God, and called onward to likeness.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: The human person
lessons.body: Human beings are the crown of the making of the world. Before Adam, the Persons take counsel: “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.” The body is formed from the ground, and then God breathes the breath of life. We are not angels housed in a costume, and we are not animals with no spirit. The honor is shown by what the Son later assumed: not an angelic nature, but ours. Every human person stands at the center of the creation God loves.

lessons.heading: Image and likeness
lessons.body: God did not make a solitary self. He made male and female, because a closed monad cannot love, and love is what the image is for. The image includes freedom. God will not force a person into good or into evil; that force would cancel the image. Likeness is the calling still ahead: Gregory of Nyssa says the limit of a life of virtue is becoming like God. You are already the image. You are not yet finished. The Christian life is the road from image to likeness, and it is walked in freedom.

lessons.heading: Soul and body
lessons.body: Christian faith agrees that the person is soul and body, and refuses the dualist conclusion that matter is evil and the body a prison. When Paul speaks of flesh warring against spirit, he is naming disordered desire, not condemning the body God made and will raise. Asceticism trains the body; it does not hate it. The end is higher than escape. The human person is called to become god by grace — not by nature, and not by leaving the body behind, but by union with God in the whole person He created.

questions.prompt: What does “Let us make” reveal about the human person?
choices: The Trinity’s counsel, and a creature made in God’s image
A bargain among the angels
That humanity is an accident of matter
questions.explanation: The Persons take counsel together. Humanity is the crown of creation, breathed into life by God.

questions.prompt: How do image and likeness differ here?
choices: The image is given, including freedom; likeness is the virtue we are called to grow into
They are opposites, and the image is lost forever
Likeness means God forces the will
questions.explanation: Freedom belongs to the image. Gregory of Nyssa: the limit of virtue is assimilation to God. God does not force the choice.

questions.prompt: What does this reading refuse about the body?
choices: That matter is originally evil and the body a prison
That soul and body are both real
That desire can be disordered
questions.explanation: Christianity rejects the dualist hatred of matter. The body is for salvation. Flesh against spirit names disordered desire, not a cursed creation.

lessonsEs.heading: La persona humana
lessonsEs.body: Los seres humanos son la corona de la hechura del mundo. Antes de Adán, las Personas se aconsejan: «Hagamos al hombre á nuestra imagen, conforme á nuestra semejanza» (Génesis 1:26, RV1909). El cuerpo se forma del suelo, y después Dios sopla el aliento de vida. No somos ángeles alojados en un disfraz, y no somos animales sin espíritu. El honor se muestra en lo que el Hijo asumió después: no una naturaleza angélica, sino la nuestra. Cada persona humana está en el centro de la creación que Dios ama.

lessonsEs.heading: Imagen y semejanza
lessonsEs.body: Dios no hizo un yo solitario. Hizo varón y mujer, porque una mónada cerrada no puede amar, y el amor es para lo que está la imagen. La imagen incluye la libertad. Dios no forzará a una persona hacia el bien ni hacia el mal; esa fuerza cancelaría la imagen. La semejanza es el llamado que todavía está adelante: Gregorio de Nisa dice que el límite de una vida de virtud es llegar a ser semejante a Dios. Ya eres la imagen. Todavía no estás terminado. La vida cristiana es el camino de la imagen a la semejanza, y se camina en libertad.

lessonsEs.body: La fe cristiana está de acuerdo en que la persona es alma y cuerpo, y rechaza la conclusión dualista de que la materia es mala y el cuerpo una prisión. Cuando Pablo habla de la carne que guerrea contra el espíritu, está nombrando el deseo desordenado, no condenando el cuerpo que Dios hizo y resucitará. El ascetismo entrena el cuerpo; no lo odia. El fin es más alto que la huida. La persona humana está llamada a llegar a ser dios por gracia: no por naturaleza, y no dejando el cuerpo atrás, sino por la unión con Dios en toda la persona que él creó.

challenges.title: Before the Fall, and the Fall
challenges.level: 2 teaching cards · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: The first humans were blessed and able to praise God. The Fall is their misuse of freedom, by pride, not a defect God built into them.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Primordial humanity before the Fall
lessons.body: A materialist picture says the first humans were simply clever animals, without God and without morality. The Church confesses the opposite: a first blessedness, a life with God in Paradise, a nature able to praise Him in words — something no other creature does. That original integrity is not a fairy tale tacked onto history. It is the memory of what we were made to be. Evil was not woven into the design. The possibility of turning away was the shadow side of a real freedom.

lessons.heading: The Fall
lessons.body: The story of the Fall is the pattern of our whole history: who we were, and what we became. Evil entered the world not because God willed it but because human beings preferred the devil’s lie to God’s command. Freedom made them the image of the Maker, and freedom held the possibility of falling. God would not override that freedom, and the devil could not force the sin. The fault is ours. Augustine names the sin as disobedience. Most of the early Fathers name it as pride: the self turning in on itself. The tree is suddenly “good for food” and “a delight to the eyes,” and God is pushed out of the center. Every generation repeats the swap — my desire first, God forgotten.

questions.prompt: What does the Church confess about the first humans?
choices: A blessed life with God, able to praise Him, not a merely bestial beginning
That God created them already fallen
That they were angels who later became animals
questions.explanation: Against the materialist picture, the faith confesses original blessedness and a real capacity to praise God.

questions.prompt: Who bears responsibility for the Fall?
choices: Human beings, who misused a freedom God would not override
God, who willed the evil
The devil, who forced them
questions.explanation: God did not will the evil and would not cancel freedom. The devil could not compel it. The misuse is human.

questions.prompt: What do most early Fathers name as Adam’s sin?
choices: Pride, the self turned inward
A lack of intelligence
The creation of the body
questions.explanation: Augustine stresses disobedience. The wider early tradition stresses pride: God is no longer the center; one’s own desire is.

lessonsEs.heading: La humanidad primordial antes de la Caída
lessonsEs.body: Un cuadro materialista dice que los primeros humanos eran simplemente animales listos, sin Dios y sin moral. La Iglesia confiesa lo contrario: una primera bienaventuranza, una vida con Dios en el Paraíso, una naturaleza capaz de alabarlo con palabras, algo que ninguna otra criatura hace. Esa integridad original no es un cuento de hadas pegado a la historia. Es la memoria de lo que fuimos hechos para ser. El mal no estaba tejido en el designio. La posibilidad de apartarse era el lado de sombra de una libertad real.

lessonsEs.heading: La Caída
lessonsEs.body: La historia de la Caída es el patrón de toda nuestra historia: quiénes éramos, y en qué nos convertimos. El mal entró en el mundo no porque Dios lo quisiera, sino porque los seres humanos prefirieron la mentira del diablo al mandamiento de Dios. La libertad los hizo imagen del Hacedor, y la libertad guardaba la posibilidad de caer. Dios no iba a anular esa libertad, y el diablo no podía forzar el pecado. La culpa es nuestra. Agustín nombra el pecado como desobediencia. La mayoría de los Padres antiguos lo nombran como soberbia: el yo volviéndose sobre sí mismo. El árbol de pronto es «bueno para comer» y «codiciable a los ojos», y Dios es empujado fuera del centro. Cada generación repite el trueque: mi deseo primero, Dios olvidado.

lessons.heading: Church as the Kingdom of Christ
lessons.body: A martyred Russian bishop wrote, at the start of the last century, that there can be no Christianity without the Church. The Church is Christ’s Kingdom, purchased by His blood. He leads into it those He has chosen, who have also chosen Him. Belonging is not a club membership beside a private faith. The person united to Christ is united to the others who are in Christ, and the house is built of those stones. Leave the Church out, and what remains is not the faith the apostles handed on.

lessons.heading: The attributes of the Church
lessons.body: “I believe in one, holy, catholic, and apostolic Church” is not a slogan. It names a divine-human organism. She is one because she is built in the image of the Trinity: unity of essence, and real persons who are not dissolved. She is holy because the Holy One dwells in her, even while her members are still being healed. She is catholic because she holds the whole faith for the whole world, not because she is merely large. She is apostolic because she continues the apostles’ teaching and mission. Christians are in patria and in via at once — already home, and still on the way. Lands that were once Christian can become mission fields again. The four marks are a confession, not a boast that the members have finished becoming holy.

questions.prompt: Why is the Church called one?
choices: She is constituted in the image of the Trinity: unity without dissolving persons
Because only one congregation exists on earth
Because disagreement is impossible
questions.explanation: Oneness images the Trinity. It is unity of life, not the claim that every member already agrees about everything.

questions.prompt: What does in patria et in via mean here?
choices: Already in the Church, and still on the way toward her fullness
Either saved or lost, with no journey
At home in the world and finished with heaven
questions.explanation: Christians are in the homeland and on the way at the same time. Holiness is given and still being lived into.

questions.prompt: What can happen to a land that was once Christian?
choices: It can need the Gospel preached again
It can never fall away
It replaces the Creed
questions.explanation: Apostolic mission is not finished. Countries can return to unbelief and need new apostles.

Es santa porque el Santo habita en ella, aun mientras sus miembros siguen siendo sanados. Es católica porque guarda la fe entera para el mundo entero, no porque sea meramente grande. Tierras que una vez fueron cristianas pueden volver a ser campos de misión. Las cuatro notas son una confesión, no un alarde de que los miembros ya terminaron de volverse santos.

challenges.title: The church hierarchy
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: From the apostles the Church has had a hierarchical priesthood: deacons, presbyters, and bishops, ordered to the Eucharist and the care of the people.

lessons.heading: The church hierarchy
lessons.body: From the beginning, some were set apart to celebrate the Eucharist and to lead. Acts 6 tells of seven deacons chosen and ordained. The threefold order — deacon, presbyter, bishop — is how the Church has received that apostolic charge. The faithful are told to honor it: deacons as servants of Christ’s commandments, bishops as those who stand in the Church in a way that Ignatius can even say “as Jesus Christ” in the sense of representing His authority, not of replacing Him. Honor is not a free pass. Paul tells Timothy, newly ordained, to be an example in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity. The hierarchy exists for the altar and the flock. A leader who will not serve has forgotten the order he was given.

questions.prompt: Why were people set apart in the apostolic Church?
choices: To celebrate the Eucharist and to lead the people

To end the need for baptism
questions.explanation: Hierarchical priesthood exists for the Eucharist and the care of the people, from the apostles onward.

questions.prompt: What does Paul require of the newly ordained Timothy?

questions.explanation: The office is to be honored, and the person who holds it is commanded to be an example.

lessonsEs.heading: La jerarquía de la Iglesia
lessonsEs.body: Desde el principio, algunos fueron apartados para celebrar la Eucaristía y para guiar. Hechos 6 cuenta de siete diáconos elegidos y ordenados. El orden triple —diácono, presbítero, obispo— es el modo en que la Iglesia ha recibido ese encargo apostólico. A los fieles se les dice que lo honren: a los diáconos como servidores de los mandamientos de Cristo, a los obispos como quienes están en la Iglesia de un modo que Ignacio puede incluso decir «como Jesucristo», en el sentido de representar su autoridad, no de reemplazarlo. El honor no es un pase libre. Pablo le dice a Timoteo, recién ordenado, que sea ejemplo en la palabra, la conducta, el amor, la fe y la pureza. La jerarquía existe para el altar y el rebaño. Un líder que no quiere servir ha olvidado el orden que se le dio.

challenges.title: Women in the Church
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: The catechism teaches why the priesthood is reserved to men, and insists that women already carry ministries the Church cannot do without.

challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Women in the Church
lessons.body: The catechism states a fact of the Church’s whole history: only men have been ordained priests and bishops. It denies that this is merely a leftover of ancient inequality. Priesthood is received as a service of spiritual fatherhood, following Christ, who chose the apostles as He did, and following the way Scripture speaks of husband and wife in Ephesians 5 — love that gives itself, and a respect that is not contempt. That is not a doctrine of women’s uselessness. Women bake the Eucharistic bread, read, sing, and carry works as necessary as those of the early deaconesses. The Mother of God is the Church’s measure of how highly a woman is honored. The argument is about the shape of the priestly office, not about the worth of women.

questions.prompt: What does this catechism claim about ordination to the priesthood and episcopate?
choices: Only men have been ordained, and this is not dismissed as a mere relic of ancient inequality

questions.explanation: The restriction is presented as the Church’s consistent practice and as a theological shape of priesthood, not as a claim that women have no ministry.

questions.prompt: Which ministries does the reading say women carry?
choices: Baking the Eucharistic bread, reading, singing, and service like that of the early deaconesses
None; women are absent from church life
Replacing the Eucharist with private prayer only
questions.explanation: The catechism names concrete, irreplaceable work. Honor of women is also measured by the Church’s honor of the Mother of God.

questions.prompt: What is the reading not saying?
choices: That women are of lesser worth as persons
That priesthood has a received shape
That Ephesians 5 speaks about marriage
questions.explanation: The argument is about the priestly office. It is not a denial of women’s dignity or of their necessary service.

lessonsEs.heading: Las mujeres en la Iglesia

Niega que esto sea meramente un resto de la desigualdad antigua. El sacerdocio se recibe como un servicio de paternidad espiritual, siguiendo a Cristo, que eligió a los apóstoles como lo hizo, y siguiendo el modo en que la Escritura habla del esposo y de la esposa en Efesios 5: un amor que se da, y un respeto que no es desprecio. Eso no es una doctrina de la inutilidad de las mujeres. Las mujeres hornean el pan eucarístico, leen, cantan y llevan obras tan necesarias como las de las diaconisas antiguas. La Madre de Dios es la medida de la Iglesia de cuán alto se honra a una mujer. El argumento es acerca de la forma del oficio sacerdotal, no acerca del valor de las mujeres.

challenges.title: Church time
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: The Church lives in time and breathes eternity. The calendar makes Christ’s life the personal experience of the people who keep it.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Church time
lessons.body: The Church is on earth and turned toward heaven; she lives in time and breathes eternity. That double life is why there is a calendar. The year, the week, and the day are not empty schedules. They are how communion with eternity is practiced. In the feasts, the events of Christ’s life become the experience of the person who is praying, not only a memory of someone else’s past. As an icon carries the presence of the one depicted, church time carries the presence of Christ, His Mother, the angels, and the saints whose memory is kept. Skip the calendar and you do not become more spiritual. You become deaf to the way the Church has learned to stand in both time and eternity.

questions.prompt: What is church time for?
choices: Communion with eternity, so that Christ’s life becomes our own experience
A way to avoid prayer
Only a record of ancient events with no presence in them
questions.explanation: The calendar is how a Church that lives in time breathes eternity. The feasts are participatory.

questions.prompt: What comparison does this reading use for feast days?
choices: Like an icon, they carry the presence of the one who is commemorated
Like a lock that keeps heaven out
Like a myth no one is meant to enter
questions.explanation: Church time is full of the presence of Christ, His Mother, the angels, and the saints, as an icon carries presence.

questions.prompt: Which pair names the Church’s life?
choices: On earth and turned toward heaven; in time and breathing eternity
Only in heaven, with no life on earth
Only in the past, with no feast still kept
questions.explanation: The Church does not choose between time and eternity. She lives in one and breathes the other.

lessonsEs.heading: El tiempo de la Iglesia
lessonsEs.body: La Iglesia está en la tierra y vuelta hacia el cielo; vive en el tiempo y respira la eternidad. Esa doble vida es la razón de que haya un calendario. El año, la semana y el día no son horarios vacíos. Son el modo en que se practica la comunión con la eternidad. En las fiestas, los acontecimientos de la vida de Cristo se vuelven la experiencia de la persona que ora, no solo un recuerdo del pasado de otro. Como un ícono lleva la presencia del representado, el tiempo de la Iglesia lleva la presencia de Cristo, de su Madre, de los ángeles y de los santos cuya memoria se guarda. Sáltate el calendario y no te vuelves más espiritual. Te vuelves sordo al modo en que la Iglesia ha aprendido a estar a la vez en el tiempo y en la eternidad.

challenges.title: The Church and the churches
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: The Creed confesses one Church. Christian divisions are real. So is the warning not to draw God’s boundaries for Him.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Divisions and reconciliation
lessons.body: The Creed says one Church. The world is full of communities that use the name and often refuse one another Communion. The early Church was severe with heresy: no shared Eucharist, no shared prayer, because Arius, Sabellius, and Eutyches denied the foundations — Christ’s divinity, the equality of the Persons, the fullness of the two natures. Most communities Christians meet today are not in that category. They accept the basic dogmas. Philaret of Moscow said that treating Catholicism as if it were Arianism is harsh and useless. Separated communities can be regarded as branches cut from the trunk, and at the same time an Orthodox Christian must not announce that God is forbidden to act outside the Orthodox Church. That would cage the Almighty. Augustine’s caution belongs with Philaret’s: on the day of judgment, some who seemed outside will be found within, and some who seemed within will not. God knows the limits of the Church. We do not get to finish His sentence.

questions.prompt: Why were ancient heresies treated so strictly?
choices: They denied foundations: Christ’s divinity, the Trinity, or the fullness of His natures
They used a different calendar only
They prayed too often
questions.explanation: Arianism, Sabellianism, and Eutychianism struck at the faith itself. That is why the canons were severe.

questions.prompt: What did St Philaret warn against?
choices: Putting Catholicism on the same footing as Arianism
Ever speaking to a non-Orthodox Christian
The Nicene Creed
questions.explanation: He called that equation rigorous and counterproductive. Non-Orthodoxy is not automatically the old heresies.

questions.prompt: What would it mean to say grace cannot exist outside the Orthodox Church?
choices: To limit God’s freedom to act
To quote the Creed accurately and stop
To honor the saints
questions.explanation: The Church confesses her own unity and still refuses to imprison God. He knows her limits. We must not pretend we have mapped them.

lessonsEs.heading: Divisiones y reconciliación
lessonsEs.body: El Credo dice una Iglesia. El mundo está lleno de comunidades que usan el nombre y a menudo se niegan unas a otras la Comunión. La Iglesia antigua fue severa con la herejía: nada de Eucaristía compartida, nada de oración compartida, porque Arrio, Sabelio y Eutiques negaban los fundamentos: la divinidad de Cristo, la igualdad de las Personas, la plenitud de las dos naturalezas. La mayoría de las comunidades que los cristianos encuentran hoy no están en esa categoría. Aceptan los dogmas básicos. Filareto de Moscú dijo que tratar el catolicismo como si fuera arrianismo es duro e inútil. Las comunidades separadas pueden mirarse como ramas cortadas del tronco, y al mismo tiempo un cristiano ortodoxo no debe anunciar que a Dios se le prohíbe actuar fuera de la Iglesia ortodoxa. Eso enjaularía al Todopoderoso. La cautela de Agustín va con la de Filareto: el día del juicio, algunos que parecían estar fuera se hallarán dentro, y algunos que parecían estar dentro no. Dios conoce los límites de la Iglesia. A nosotros no nos toca terminar su frase.

Dios conoce los límites de la Iglesia. A nosotros no nos toca terminar su frase.

challenges.title: A life in the sacraments
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: A sacrament is an encounter: a visible rite and a material gift, and an invisible rebirth of the whole person, body and soul.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: A life in the sacraments
lessons.body: The sacraments are sacred actions in which God and a person meet. Grace descends and sanctifies. The Orthodox Church speaks of seven — Baptism, Chrismation, Eucharist, Penance, Anointing, Marriage, and Priesthood — and treats other sacred actions as rites. That numbering was learned from Latin scholasticism. The Fathers of the first millennium did not anxiously count. What they did know is the shape of each mystery: a visible side (words, gestures, and a material — water, bread, wine, oil) and an invisible side, the person’s transfiguration, which is the mystery proper. The body is not left outside. Immersion, anointing, and communion are bodily because the body is meant for salvation and deification. In the age to come the material signs will no longer be needed in the same way. Here, they are how God gives Himself to people who are still body and soul.

questions.prompt: What is the invisible side of a sacrament?
choices: The person’s spiritual and bodily transfiguration, beyond what the senses can measure
Only the words printed in the book
A feeling the priest must manufacture
questions.explanation: The rite and the material are visible. The mystery is the hidden rebirth of the person for whom the rite is done.

questions.prompt: Where did the practice of numbering seven sacraments come from, in this reading?
choices: It was borrowed from Latin scholasticism; the early Fathers did not fix a number
It is a list written by the apostles as a closed count
It excludes baptism
questions.explanation: Seven is the Church’s received practice now. The catechism is honest that counting them was a later, Western habit. The mysteries themselves are not late.

questions.prompt: Why does the body take part?
choices: Because the body, too, is destined for salvation and deification
Because the soul is irrelevant
Because matter is evil and must be displayed
questions.explanation: Immersion, anointing, and communion are bodily on purpose. The whole person enters the gift.

lessonsEs.heading: Una vida en los sacramentos
lessonsEs.body: Los sacramentos son acciones sagradas en las que Dios y una persona se encuentran. La gracia desciende y santifica. La Iglesia ortodoxa habla de siete —Bautismo, Crismación, Eucaristía, Penitencia, Unción, Matrimonio y Sacerdocio— y trata otras acciones sagradas como ritos. Esa numeración se aprendió de la escolástica latina. Los Padres del primer milenio no contaban con ansiedad. Lo que sí conocían es la forma de cada misterio: un lado visible (palabras, gestos y una materia: agua, pan, vino, aceite) y un lado invisible, la transfiguración de la persona, que es el misterio propiamente dicho. El cuerpo no se deja fuera. La inmersión, la unción y la comunión son corporales porque el cuerpo está destinado a la salvación y a la deificación. En el siglo venidero los signos materiales ya no se necesitarán del mismo modo. Aquí son el modo en que Dios se da a personas que todavía son cuerpo y alma.

challenges.title: Baptism
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Baptism is the door into the Church. It is new birth in Christ for the whole of life, from infancy to old age.

challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Baptism
lessons.body: Baptism is the door into the Church, the Kingdom of grace, and the frontier between those who are in Christ’s Body and those still outside. Christian life begins here, not after a probation. The person is clothed in Christ. Irenaeus says Christ came to save, through rebirth in God, infants, children, adolescents, and the elderly — the whole age of the race, not a class of adults who have already understood everything. The grace given in the water is a pledge and a seed. It grows where a person struggles toward Christ, lives in the Church, and keeps the commandments. Baptism is not magic that replaces that life, and life does not replace baptism. The door and the road belong together.

questions.prompt: Whom does Irenaeus say Christ saves through rebirth?
choices: Infants, children, adolescents, and the elderly
Only adults who can explain the Creed
Only monks
questions.explanation: The whole span of human age is included. Rebirth is not restricted to those who already understand.

questions.prompt: What is the grace of Baptism compared to?
choices: A seed or pledge that grows when the person lives toward Christ in the Church
A finished castle that needs no obedience
A feeling that fades and leaves nothing
questions.explanation: The gift is real at the font and is meant to grow in a life of faithfulness.

lessonsEs.heading: El bautismo
lessonsEs.body: El bautismo es la puerta a la Iglesia, el Reino de la gracia, y la frontera entre quienes están en el Cuerpo de Cristo y quienes todavía están fuera. La vida cristiana empieza aquí, no después de un período de prueba. La persona es revestida de Cristo. Ireneo dice que Cristo vino a salvar, por el nuevo nacimiento en Dios, a infantes, niños, adolescentes y ancianos: toda la edad de la raza, no una clase de adultos que ya lo entendieron todo. La gracia dada en el agua es una prenda y una semilla. Crece donde una persona lucha hacia Cristo, vive en la Iglesia y guarda los mandamientos. El bautismo no es magia que reemplace esa vida, y la vida no reemplaza el bautismo. La puerta y el camino van juntos.

challenges.title: Chrismation

lessons.heading: Chrismation
lessons.body: In the apostles’ days, the newly baptized received the Holy Spirit by the laying on of hands. Acts shows Peter and John doing this for the Samaritans who had been baptized but had not yet received the Spirit in that way. The Church continues that gift by holy chrism, consecrated by the bishop, so that the Spirit’s seal is not limited to the places an apostle can stand. Alexander Schmemann’s distinction is the one to keep: this is not one charism among others. It is the Holy Spirit Himself, given as a gift. The gift can be neglected. Every sacrament saves in the life that agrees with it. Chrismation is Pentecost made personal, not a ceremony with no aftermath.

questions.prompt: What apostolic action does Chrismation continue?
choices: The laying on of hands for the gift of the Holy Spirit
The election of a king
A replacement for baptism
questions.explanation: Acts shows the apostles laying hands on the newly baptized. Chrism continues that gift.

questions.prompt: What is given, in Schmemann’s explanation?
choices: The Holy Spirit Himself, not merely one gift among others
Only a symbol with no Giver
A talent for preaching and nothing more
questions.explanation: The seal is the Spirit as gift. Particular charisms are a different subject.

questions.prompt: When does the gift do its saving work?
choices: When the Christian’s life agrees with what was received
Automatically, no matter how one lives
Only if Chrismation is repeated yearly
questions.explanation: The catechism ties every sacrament’s fruit to a life in harmony with the gift.

Hechos muestra a Pedro y a Juan haciendo esto por los samaritanos que habían sido bautizados pero todavía no habían recibido el Espíritu de ese modo. La Iglesia continúa ese don con el santo crisma, consagrado por el obispo, para que el sello del Espíritu no se limite a los lugares donde un apóstol puede estar de pie. La distinción de Alejandro Schmemann es la que hay que guardar: esto no es un carisma entre otros. Es el Espíritu Santo mismo, dado como don. El don puede descuidarse. Cada sacramento salva en la vida que concuerda con él. La crismación es Pentecostés hecho personal, no una ceremonia sin consecuencia.

challenges.title: Penance
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Christianity opens with a call to repentance. In confession the priest is a witness; God is the one who forgives and heals.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Penance
lessons.body: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” John the Baptist began there, and so did Jesus. Christianity is a call to metanoia, a change of mind, not a small regret. The obvious question is why tell one’s sins to a priest. The answer in this reading is that the priest is a witness of God’s presence. God Himself acts. The priest does not manufacture forgiveness and does not stand in God’s place as a rival. Confession also heals by light. While a soul stays a dark room, sins remain unrecognized and therefore unhealed. Spoken repentance is how the room is opened. The kingdom’s nearness and the honesty of confession belong to the same invitation.

questions.prompt: What does metanoia mean in this reading?
choices: A change of mind, a real conversion

A public speech with no repentance
questions.explanation: Repentance is a change of mind. It is how the Gospel begins, in both John and Jesus.

questions.prompt: Who acts in the sacrament of Penance?

No one; confession is only a conversation
questions.explanation: The priest does not replace God. He witnesses what God does.

questions.prompt: Why do unspoken sins stay unhealed?
choices: While they stay in the dark they stay unrecognized
Because God cannot hear thoughts
Because only public punishment heals
questions.explanation: The image is a dark room. What is never brought to light is never treated.

lessonsEs.heading: La penitencia
lessonsEs.body: «Arrepentíos, que el reino de los cielos se ha acercado» (Mateo 3:2; 4:17, RV1909). Juan el Bautista empezó ahí, y Jesús también. El cristianismo es un llamado a la metanoia, un cambio de mente, no un arrepentimiento pequeño. La pregunta obvia es por qué decir los pecados a un sacerdote. La respuesta en esta lectura es que el sacerdote es testigo de la presencia de Dios. Dios mismo actúa. El sacerdote no fabrica el perdón y no se pone en el lugar de Dios como rival. La confesión también sana con la luz. Mientras un alma sigue siendo un cuarto oscuro, los pecados permanecen no reconocidos y por eso sin sanar. El arrepentimiento dicho en voz alta es el modo en que se abre el cuarto. La cercanía del reino y la honestidad de la confesión pertenecen a la misma invitación.

challenges.title: Anointing with oil
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: The body was made incorruptible and became mortal. Anointing is the Church’s prayer for the sick, body and soul together.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Anointing with oil
lessons.body: The human body was created incorruptible and immortal. After the Fall it became subject to decay and death. Gregory the Theologian can speak of our “coarse flesh” as the garment sin put on us — not because the body is trash, but because mortality is a wound. James gives the Church her answer at the bedside: call the presbyters, let them pray, anoint with oil in the Lord’s name. The prayer of faith will save the sick; the Lord will raise him up; if he has sinned, he will be forgiven. Healing and forgiveness are one visit. Sometimes the illness ends in death anyway, and even then it can turn a life toward repentance. The sacrament does not promise that every sick person will stand up. It promises that the Church will not leave body or soul unprayed.

questions.prompt: What happened to the body after the Fall, in this reading?
choices: It lost incorruption and immortality and became subject to death
It became evil by nature and should be escaped
It stayed exactly as it was in Paradise
questions.explanation: Mortality is a wound of the Fall. The body itself remains God’s creation, meant for healing.

questions.prompt: What does James tell the sick to do?
choices: Call the elders to pray and anoint with oil in the Lord’s name
Hide the illness from the Church
Seek forgiveness only, never prayer for the body
questions.explanation: James 5 joins prayer, oil, healing, and forgiveness. The presbyters come to the sick.

questions.prompt: What can illness become, even when it leads to death?
choices: A path of repentance toward God
Proof that God has abandoned the person
A reason to refuse the sacrament
questions.explanation: Not every illness ends in recovery. It can still turn a life around. The Church prays either way.

lessonsEs.heading: La unción con aceite
lessonsEs.body: El cuerpo humano fue creado incorruptible e inmortal. Después de la caída quedó sujeto a la corrupción y a la muerte. Gregorio el Teólogo puede hablar de nuestra “carne tosca” como el vestido que el pecado nos puso: no porque el cuerpo sea basura, sino porque la mortalidad es una herida. Santiago le da a la Iglesia la respuesta junto a la cama del enfermo: “¿Está alguno enfermo entre vosotros? llame á los ancianos de la iglesia, y oren por él, ungiéndole con aceite en el nombre del Señor. Y la oración de fe salvará al enfermo, y el Señor lo levantará; y si estuviere en pecados, le serán perdonados” (Santiago 5:14–15, RV1909). La sanación y el perdón llegan en la misma visita. A veces la enfermedad termina en muerte de todos modos, y aun así puede volver una vida hacia el arrepentimiento. El sacramento no promete que toda persona enferma se va a levantar. Promete que la Iglesia no va a dejar sin oración ni el cuerpo ni el alma.

challenges.title: Marriage
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Scripture’s holy couples, and the wedding at Cana, show marriage as a miracle: daily life turned into festival, and a child who is the fruit of love.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Marriage
lessons.body: Scripture lingers on the love of husband and wife: Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, Jacob and Rachel, and the blessing that rests on those unions. A human being is meant to be the fruit of love, not of use. Christian marriage asks God to crown that love and to make the home a small church. At the wedding the Church reads Cana, where water became wine, because marriage is that kind of miracle: the water of ordinary days turned into the wine of a feast that does not run out. The catechism does not romanticize every feeling. It treats faithful love as a way of salvation, beside the other ways, when two people will walk it to the end.

questions.prompt: Why is the wedding at Cana read at a Christian marriage?
choices: Marriage is the miracle of ordinary life turned into festival, as water became wine
To say Jesus discouraged marriage
To replace the couple’s vows with a parable about money
questions.explanation: Cana is the image: daily water becomes the wine of a feast. Marriage is that transformation under God’s blessing.

questions.prompt: What should a person’s birth be, in this reading?
choices: The fruit of love between the parents
An accident outside of blessing
The end of the parents’ salvation
questions.explanation: Love is not decoration. A human being is meant to come from love that God blesses.

questions.prompt: Which couples does the reading hold up from Genesis?
choices: Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, Jacob and Rachel
Adam alone, with no Eve
Only kings who never married
questions.explanation: Genesis’ holy couples are the pattern the Church blesses, not a contrast to Christian marriage.

lessonsEs.heading: El matrimonio
lessonsEs.body: La Escritura se detiene en el amor del esposo y la esposa: Abraham y Sara, Isaac y Rebeca, Jacob y Raquel, y la bendición que descansa sobre esas uniones. Un ser humano está llamado a ser fruto del amor, no del uso. El matrimonio cristiano le pide a Dios que corone ese amor y que haga de la casa una iglesia pequeña. En la boda la Iglesia lee Caná, donde el agua se hizo vino, porque el matrimonio es un milagro de ese tipo: el agua de los días ordinarios convertida en el vino de una fiesta que no se acaba. El catecismo no romantiza cada sentimiento. Trata el amor fiel como un camino de salvación, junto a los otros caminos, cuando dos personas están dispuestas a recorrerlo hasta el final.

challenges.title: Priesthood
challenges.level: 1 teaching card · 3 questions · Match the Word
challenges.summary: Ordination is a sacrament in three degrees: bishop, priest, and deacon. It is God’s act, not a license to give speeches.
challenges.source: The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev
challenges.adaptation: Adapted from The Mystery of Faith by Bishop Hilarion Alfeyev.

lessons.heading: Priesthood
lessons.body: The sacrament of priesthood is conferred in three rites: to the episcopate, to the priesthood, and to the diaconate. In present Orthodox practice bishops are chosen from the monks. The early Church also had married bishops; the later discipline is a received rule of life, not a denial that marriage is holy. At the ordination the Church sings “Lord, have mercy” while the bishop reads the prayers. The point of those prayers is that the gift comes from God. A contrast makes it sharp: in some Protestant settings the only difference between lay and ordained is a license to preach. Orthodox ordination is not that. It sets a man at the altar to offer the Eucharist and to shepherd, by a gift he cannot give himself.

questions.prompt: What are the three rites of the sacrament of priesthood?
choices: Ordination to the episcopate, the priesthood, and the diaconate
Baptism, marriage, and burial
A license, a contract, and a vote
questions.explanation: One sacrament, three degrees. Each is conferred by ordination, not by a preaching permit.

questions.prompt: What does this reading say about married bishops?
choices: The early Church had them; choosing bishops from the monks is a later discipline
Marriage was always forbidden to every clergyman including deacons
Bishops were never ordained at all
questions.explanation: The catechism distinguishes present monastic practice for bishops from the early Church’s married bishops. Marriage itself is not despised.

questions.prompt: What is ordination not, in the contrast drawn here?
choices: Only a license to preach
A prayer in which God gives the gift
A setting apart for the Eucharist
questions.explanation: The Orthodox rite asks God for a gift. It is more than permission to speak.

lessonsEs.heading: El sacerdocio
lessonsEs.body: El sacramento del sacerdocio se confiere en tres ritos: al episcopado, al presbiterado y al diaconado. En la práctica ortodoxa de hoy los obispos se eligen de entre los monjes. La Iglesia antigua también tuvo obispos casados; la disciplina posterior es una regla de vida recibida, no una negación de que el matrimonio sea santo. En la ordenación la Iglesia canta “Señor, ten piedad” mientras el obispo lee las oraciones. El sentido de esas oraciones es que el don viene de Dios. Un contraste lo deja claro: en algunos ámbitos protestantes la única diferencia entre el laico y el ordenado es un permiso para predicar. La ordenación ortodoxa no es eso. Pone a un hombre en el altar para ofrecer la Eucaristía y para pastorear, por un don que él no puede darse a sí mismo.
